attorneys.name: Philip A. Bareck
attorneys.firm_name: Katz, Friedman, Eisenstein, Johnson, Bareck & Bertuca
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Law Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
Philip A. Bareck has been with Katz Friedman since 1991, became a partner in 2003, and a shareholder in 2007. Currently, he is an Adjunct Professor at IIT Chicago-Kent College of Law teaching Workers' Compensation Law and was recently inducted into the College of Workers Compensation Lawyers in New Orleans, Louisiana. He continues to be selected as an Illinois Super Lawyer (5% of the attorneys in Illinois), included in Best Lawyers in Workers’ Compensation Law, awarded inclusion in Top Trial Lawyers (American Trial Lawyers Association top 100 Trial Lawyers for Illinois), Top Attorneys in Illinois, selected as one of America’s Most Honored Professionals, nominated as “10 Best” Workers’ Compensation Attorneys for Illinois by the American Institute of Legal Counsel (AIOLC) and selected by his peers to be a Leading Lawyer in Workers' Compensation Law (fewer than 5% of all licensed attorneys in Illinois).

His practice concentrates in representing injured employees in Workers’ Compensation and Occupational Disease cases before the Workers’ Compensation Commission, Illinois Circuit, and Appellate courts. He has successfully represented thousands of individuals with a vast array of injuries and has deposed hundreds of physicians in order to protect and preserve his clients’ rights and entitlements. Moreover, he has secured future medical rights and ongoing treatment for his clients requiring long-term care. Philip has spent his career fighting against Caterpillar, Fiat-Chrysler, Knapheide, the State of Illinois/Illinois Veterans Home, UTC Hamilton-Sundstrand, AT&T, Comcast, Gardner-Denver Machinery, Mueller Company, Ipsen, Inc., Home Depot, most of the employers in Quincy, Illinois and other large and aggressive companies throughout the state of Illinois. In 2016, he won a significant Appellate Court decision in Dunteman v. Caterpillar in which the Court found that an employee’s self-treatment, at home, for a work-related injury, which worsened the condition, still remained covered by the Illinois Workers’ Compensation Act. He has spoken to various lawyer groups concerning the Dunteman impact in Illinois and was interviewed and quoted in Work Comp Central concerning the Dunteman decision.

Philip has been a regular speaker/faculty member on workers’ compensation topics for the Illinois Institute of Continuing Legal Education (IICLE) seminars, presented at the Chicago Bar Association, Rockford Bar Association and is a frequent speaker at Union meetings, Retiree meetings, and Labor Law/Workers’ Compensation Workshops in Illinois. He traveled the state as a speaker/presenter on the 2011 Illinois Workers’ Compensation Reform, authored an article captioned “Workers’ Compensation Reform Arrives” in the September 14, 2011 Chicago Daily Law Bulletin, and was quoted in the Chicago Tribune Business Section concerning the 2011 changes to the Illinois Workers’ Compensation Act.

Phil Bareck has written faculty material for IICLE presentations on Deposition Practice, Permanent Partial Disability Recoveries, Utilization review under the Illinois Workers’ Compensation Act, Review/Appeal Process, Permanent and Total Disability, Wage Loss Cases in Illinois, Landmine Issues in Settlement of Cases and Payments of Fees, and Presenting a Case for Arbitration Hearing – Petitioner’s Perspective, among other topics. In addition, he has authored “Physical, Mental and Vocational Rehabilitation Under the Illinois Workers’ Compensation Act”, “Establishing Accident: The Arising Out of the Employment Element” and “Advanced Workers’ Compensation in Illinois” and has published an article in the Summer, 2007 Illinois Trial Journal captioned “Jurisdiction in Illinois Workers’ Compensation Cases: The 2006 Mahoney Decision.”

He earned his undergraduate degree at the University of Illinois in 1988 and obtained his law degree from IIT Chicago-Kent College of Law with High Honors in 1991. He was taught workers’ compensation law by Warren Eagle, who was an adjunct professor at the law school and was Philip’s mentor and partner until his retirement in 2010. Philip continues to be very active politically in his community and is a staunch advocate for injured workers’ benefits, union members’ rights and protecting victims of accidents and injuries. He is married to Margaret, his law school sweetheart, and they have three children who are all on their way to becoming fellow attorneys.

He has spoken to various lawyer groups concerning the Dunteman impact in Illinois and was interviewed and quoted in Work Comp Central concerning the Dunteman decision.

Philip has been a regular speaker/faculty member on workers’ compensation topics for the Illinois Institute of Continuing Legal Education (IICLE) seminars, presented at the Chicago Bar Association, Rockford Bar Association and is a frequent speaker at Union meetings, Retiree meetings, and Labor Law/Workers’ Compensation Workshops in Illinois. He traveled the state as a speaker/presenter on the 2011 Illinois Workers’ Compensation Reform, authored an article captioned “Workers’ Compensation Reform Arrives” in the September 14, 2011 Chicago Daily Law Bulletin, and was quoted in the Chicago Tribune Business Section concerning the 2011 changes to the Illinois Workers’ Compensation Act.

Phil Bareck has written faculty material for IICLE presentations on Deposition Practice, Permanent Partial Disability Recoveries, Utilization review under the Illinois Workers’ Compensation Act, Review/Appeal Process, Permanent and Total Disability, Wage Loss Cases in Illinois, Landmine Issues in Settlement of Cases and Payments of Fees, and Presenting a Case for Arbitration Hearing – Petitioner’s Perspective, among other topics. In addition, he has authored “Physical, Mental and Vocational Rehabilitation Under the Illinois Workers’ Compensation Act”, “Establishing Accident: The Arising Out of the Employment Element” and “Advanced Workers’ Compensation in Illinois” and has published an article in the Summer, 2007 Illinois Trial Journal captioned “Jurisdiction in Illinois Workers’ Compensation Cases: The 2006 Mahoney Decision.”

He earned his undergraduate degree at the University of Illinois in 1988 and obtained his law degree from IIT Chicago-Kent College of Law with High Honors in 1991. He was taught workers’ compensation law by Warren Eagle, who was an adjunct professor at the law school and was Philip’s mentor and partner until his retirement in 2010. Philip continues to be very active politically in his community and is a staunch advocate for injured workers’ benefits, union members’ rights and protecting victims of accidents and injuries. He is married to Margaret, his law school sweetheart, and they have three children who are all on their way to becoming fellow attorneys.

attorneys.name: David M. Barish
attorneys.firm_name: Katz, Friedman, Eisenstein, Johnson, Bareck & Bertuca
attorneys.practice_type: Labor and Employment Law Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
David M. Barish joined Katz Friedman in the fall of 2001. He covers cases that are set in Chicago, Rockford, Woodstock, Waukegan, Elgin, Wheaton, Geneva and New Lenox. He is available to meet clients at many locations in northern Illinois. David has tried cases against Chrysler and the supplier plants to the Belvidere Assembly including Grupo Antolin, Android and Syncreon.

David is fluent in Spanish and works with a paralegal who is also a fluent Spanish speaker. He has also represented many Polish speaking clients. During the course of his four-decade career he has practiced workers’ compensation law across the state of Illinois and has argued many cases before the Appellate Court of Illinois including Illinois Armored Car v. Industrial Commission, David has an AV, preeminent rating from Martindale Hubbell and a perfect 10 rating from Avvo. He has been recognized as one of Illinois’ Leading Lawyers.

A gifted teacher and public speaker, he has presented and moderated seminars on a variety of workers’ compensation topics for the Illinois State Bar Association, Chicago Bar Association, Illinois Institute of Continuing Legal Education, National Business Institute and other organizations on a variety of workers’ compensation topics including evidence, jurisdiction, whether an accident arises out of and in the course of employment, and trial strategy. He distinguished himself by achieving high ratings from the reviews he has received for these presentations. He has been a lecturer at the Illinois Workers’ Compensation Commission’s arbitrator training. He has been the moderator and co-coordinator for the Illinois Institute of Continuing Legal Education’s Workers’ Compensation Institute since 2014.

David has been representing claimants for Social Security Disability and Supplemental Security Income for over 30 years. He has had hearings all over the State of Illinois and has represented many clients in Hannibal, Missouri just across the river from Quincy, Illinois.

Prior to his affiliation with Katz Friedman, David was a principal at another firm in Chicago where he represented employers and employees in workers’ compensation, social security, and longshoremen’s cases. While at that firm David presented at many client seminars and helped create those educational programs for the firm. He hired that firm’s law student clerks and does the same for Katz, Friedman. David continues to represent injured workers and social security disability claimants as a trial attorney at Katz Friedman. He is an active member of the Workers’ Compensation Lawyer’s Association. He was a member of the Illinois State Bar Association, where he was been a member of the Workers’ Compensation Section Council and served as chair of that Section Council from 2009 to 2010. David graduated from Northwestern University in 1980 with a Bachelor of Science in Speech majoring in Communication Studies. He earned his Juris Doctor from DePaul College of Law in 1983. As a Senior Law Student authorized by Illinois Supreme Court rule, David tried more than 50 criminal cases, including a jury trial, for Public Defender of Cook County. Before attending law school he was a member of Teamsters Local 703 when he worked for a fruit company on Chicago’s South Watermarket. He was sworn in before the Illinois Bar in November 1983.

An avid bicycle enthusiast, David commutes to his office on two-wheels when he is not driving a UAW made automobile. David has been involved in cycling advocacy. He is a former President of the Evanston Bicycle club, a member of the Skokie Bike Network, and is a widely respected ride leader. When not writing briefs on behalf of his clients David has written and published personal essays. He is a highly regarded storyteller on the Chicago live literature scene. He lives in the Chicago area with his wife, a writer and writing coach. They have two adult daughters.

attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Edwardsville, IL
attorneys.bio:
John Baricevic received his undergraduate degree from St. Benedicts College in Atchison, Kansas, a Masters degree from Kansas State Teachers College and completed his law degree at Southern Illinois University - Carbondale.

Mr. Baricevic served as Assistant State’s Attorney in St. Clair County from 1978-1980 and was elected St. Clair County State’s Attorney from 1980-1990. In 1990, he was elected St. Clair County Board Chairman, an office he held until 2004 when he was elected Circuit Judge. He served as Chief Judge from 2006-2016 and served on numerous committees including Probation Services and the Illinois Supreme Courts Committee on Opiate Addiction.

Throughout his career Mr. Baricevic has served as President of the Illinois States Attorneys Association, Vice President of the National District Attorneys Association and as a member of the Illinois Senate select committee on County Funding. He also served as Chairman of East-West Gateway and the Metro Counties Council. As a member he served Civic Progress, Leadership Council Southwestern Illinois, St. Louis Regional Chamber and Growth Association, United Way, Belleville Chamber of Commerce, the Committee to Retain and Enhance Scott AFB and led the building of light rail in St. Clair County. He has also served as President of the St. Clair County and East St. Louis Bar Associations and is a member of the Illinois State Bar.

attorneys.name: Jason Barnes
attorneys.practice_type: Complex Litigation Lawyers in Alton, IL
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Jason “Jay” Barnes is a partner at Simmons Hanly Conroy in the Complex Litigation Department where he focuses his practice on consumer class action lawsuits. Before joining the firm, Jay served eight years as a state representative in the Missouri General Assembly. In this role, he fought against fraud, abuse and waste as chairman of the House Committee on Government Oversight and Accountability. He also served as chairman of the Special Investigative Committee on Oversight formed in 2018 to investigate the wrongdoings of former Missouri governor Eric Greitens.

As a shareholder at the firm, Jay represents hardworking people who have been wronged through corporate fraud.

“I love representing everyday people against corporations who have abused their power and committed fraud,” Jay said. “Consumer class action practice often requires a great deal of diligence in order to be successful, and I am always up for the challenge.”

Working with Jay

Jay utilizes a mixture of experience, dedication, professionalism and tenacity to secure justice on behalf of his clients. Using this valuable skill set, he puts clients at ease with the often-complicated legal process, ensuring their questions and concerns are addressed quickly and with care. This has translated to a wealth of success for Jay and his clients, securing millions of dollars in settlements on their behalf.

“When a client hires me, they get everything I’ve got,” Jay said. “I will be a fearless, conscientious and caring champion for their case against the person or company that harmed them. They can count on that.”

Experience in Missouri’s Government

During Jay’s eight years as a state representative, he was instrumental in passing legislation that protected the lives and rights of Missourians from all walks of life. Through these bills and amendments, he protected student athletes from concussions; increased adoptee rights; increase access to healthcare for foster children and persons with disabilities; protected senior citizens from financial fraud; expanded college scholarship opportunities for students in parochial schools; prohibit internet extortion; fought corruption by prohibiting legislators from immediately becoming lobbyists after their term is completed; and created an avenue through with Missourians can expunge past criminal convictions after they have served their sentence, helping them to once again become productive members of society.

In early 2018, Jay’s focus was largely focused with the investigation into Greitens’ misconduct. After the former governor’s resignation, Jay received praise for his bipartisan professionalism that led him to uncover the truth.

In an editorial published in the Kansas City Star, the paper’s editors were quick to bolster this praise.

“Rep. Jay Barnes and other members of the committee he led deserved special credit for handling this difficult task with complete professionalism […] Missourians owe a debt to Barnes, and all the members of the Greitens committee, for their hard work, seriousness of purpose, transparency and bipartisan approach,” the editorial read.

Noteworthy Cases

As one of the nation’s leading consumer-privacy attorneys, Jay has argued several notable cases in recent history that are representative of his vast experience and track record of success:

In re: Google Cookie, 806 F.3d 125 (3d Cir. 2015) – Established precedent that common law intrusion upon seclusion is actionable against Internet companies that mislead consumers about privacy practices. Settlement pending.

In re: Nickelodeon Consumer Privacy Litigation, 827 F.3d 262 (3d Cir. 2016) – Following Google Cookie, established first post-Spokeo precedent that privacy injury is sufficient to confer Art. III standing. Confidential settlement.

Fernandez v. Atkins Nutritionals, Inc., S.D. Cal.; Smith v. Atkins Nutritionals, Inc., W.D. Mo.; Colella v. Atkins Nutritionals, Inc., E.D. N.Y. – Consumer fraud claims against food manufacturer for misrepresentations of product health qualities. Cases ongoing.

Janson v. LegalZoom, 802 F.Supp.2d 1053 (W.D. Mo. 2011) – Unauthorized practice of law. Settlement for $7.8 million and injunctive relief requiring actual attorneys to review and have involvement with certain business practices.

An Award-winning Attorney

Jay’s accomplishments are well-documented not only through verdicts, settlements and press clippings, but also through the awards and accolades he’s received from his peers and community. A small sampling of notable honors include:

Influential Lawyer Award, Missouri Lawyers Weekly, 2019

Champion of Justice Award, Missouri Association of Trial Attorneys, 2018

State Advocate of the Year Award, St. Louis Children’s Hospital, 2015

Rory Ellinger Legislative Award, The Legal Services of Eastern Missouri, 2015

Legislator of the Year Award, Missouri Bar Association, 2014

attorneys.name: John A. Barnerd
attorneys.practice_type: Mesothelioma and Asbestos Lawyers in Alton, IL
attorneys.bio:
John Barnerd is a partner at Simmons Hanly Conroy. He joined the firm in 2002 as mesothelioma and asbestos attorney, and today is a member of the firm’s management committee. He previously served for two years as an Assistant State’s Attorney for Madison County, Ill.

John earned his bachelor’s degree in accounting from Illinois College and graduated with his J.D. from Saint Louis University School of Law. In 2010, Chicago Lawyers Magazine recognized him as a top 40 Under 40 Illinois Attorney. For the past four years, he has been named a Rising Star by Super Lawyers Magazine.

John grew up in East Alton, Ill., a manufacturing community in which many people he knew became sick from asbestos exposure.

“That’s probably one of the reasons why I am an asbestos trial attorney. There’s a personal connection,” he said.

John negotiates with asbestos defendants on behalf of the firm’s clients. His work has helped secure millions of dollars on behalf of asbestos exposure victims and families.

Leveling the Playing Field

John has worked with hundreds of people diagnosed with mesothelioma and other asbestos-related diseases, who decided to hold the companies that harmed them accountable.

“As an everyday blue collar worker, going up against a multinational billion dollar company can seem a daunting prospect,” said John. “But with Simmons Hanly Conroy, they get a team of experienced mesothelioma litigators who give them compassionate personalized service, and they get access to resources that have leveled the playing field against these big companies time and time again.”

Over the past 10 years, John has cultivated a keen understanding of asbestos cases. Most importantly, he knows each case is different because no person is alike, and neither are their lives.

“No two people have lived the exact same life and been exposed to the same products,” he said. “Recognizing that helps me build a better case for my clients, instead of just a cookie cutter approach.”

John has been invited to speak on several legal panels as an asbestos expert. Notable appearances include the Mesothelioma Applied Research Foundation’s first ever Legal Panel during the 2011 International Symposium on Malignant Mesothelioma, co-chair of the Midwest Asbestos Litigation Conference in St. Louis and presentations during the Plaintiffs’ Asbestos Litigation Conference in Los Angeles.

attorneys.name: Caryn A. Barone
attorneys.firm_name: Soffietti, Johnson, Teegen, Argueta, Bawcum & Barone
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Waukegan, IL
attorneys.bio:
Caryn began her start in the Lake County legal community when as a Lake County Assistant State's Attorney in October of 2007. During her seven and a half years in the Office, Caryn handled DUIs, traffic cases, misdemeanors, domestic violence cases and felony cases including serious sex crimes and murders. During her tenure with the Lake County State's Attorney's Office Caryn developed an excellent reputation with all sides of the legal community, including police officers, Defense Attorneys, Prosecutors and Judges, as someone who is not only fair and just, but also as an attorney who is not afraid to go to trial. As an Assistant State's Attorney, Caryn tried over 70 cases to verdict and is known for being able to think on her feet and execute effective cross examinations.

Caryn took the reputation and skill set she built with the State's Attorney's Office with her to the law firm of Soffietti, Johnson, Teegen, Phillips and Argueta LTD in January of 2015, where she is the Village Prosecutor for the all traffic, ordinance violations and DUIs for the Village of Fox Lake. Caryn also handles traffic, criminal and DUI cases. Caryn's ability to evaluate the strengths and weaknesses of a case and decide which cases should go to trial and which cases need to be resolved is an asset as a Defense Attorney.

Caryn heads the firm's Family Law and Divorce practice including child support matters, parentage actions, divorces, orders of protection and post decree matters. Caryn has been on the Lake County Guardian Ad Litem list since 2016 where she is appointed by the Court to represent the best interests of minor children involved in divorce, parentage and order of protection situation. Caryn's litigation skill set and experience provides her with an edge in Family Law and Divorce cases.

Caryn was named partner January 1, 2020.

Caryn utilizes the support staff at Soffietti, Johnson,Teegen, Argueta, Bawcum & Barone LTD. to take on Spanish speaking clients and is able to communicate with them to the fullest extent on their cases.

attorneys.name: Jesse V. Barrientes Esq.
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Offices of Jesse V. Barrientes
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Wheaton, IL
attorneys.bio:
A child custody case, divorce or other legal family matters do not always have to be upsetting or an antagonistic experience. When the issues are intricate, and the future is in doubt, I will work hard to protect your legal rights while avoiding unnecessary conflict and stress. However, if litigation is required, I will fight for your rights in a court of law.

As a skilled Wheaton Illinois Divorce Lawyer, my goal is to resolve matters quickly, to save clients the financial and emotional trauma of litigation.

The law firm you choose is critical to the success of your case. My Firm provides aggressive, experienced and quality legal services. As a respected Wheaton Illinois Divorce Lawyer, I focus on the equitable and financially feasible resolution of your legal situation. I do not believe in sugar-coating my advice, or telling clients what they want to hear simply so that they will retain me. I believe that each client must be aware of the realities of their unique legal situation, and the ramifications of their various legal options in order to render an intelligent, informed, and reasoned decision. I believe in keeping clients informed of the status and progress of their case at each and every stage of litigation.

If you or someone you know is involved in a divorce or child custody case and needs the assistance of an experienced Wheaton Illinois Divorce Lawyer, call Attorney Jesse V. Barrientes today or complete the contact form provided on this site to schedule your free consultation.

attorneys.bio:
Mathias Bartlett pursued his law degree at Tulane Law School in New Orleans in 2017, where he also received certifications in environmental law, arbitration, mediation, and negotiation.

Mr. Bartlett began his legal career as a public defender in Portland, Oregon. He then worked for criminal defense firms, where he developed a passion for family law. While providing legal support to families, Mr. Bartlett gained robust experience handling delicate issues such as divorce, child custody, spousal support, and property division. This then transformed into a desire to offer guidance to clients navigating complex legal situations associated with complications and illnesses associated with asbestos exposure.

Today, Mr. Bartlett assists clients out of The Gori Law Firm’s New York City office. His practice is focused primarily on asbestos litigation.

attorneys.name: Juan P. Bauta II
attorneys.practice_type: Asbestos & Mesothelioma Lawyers in Alton, IL
attorneys.bio:
Juan P. Bauta is a class action and mesothelioma attorney at Simmons Hanly Conroy. He is based in the firm’s Florida office and has over 30 years of experience helping clients seek justice.

Juan strives to make the legal process as easy and stress-free as possible for those he represents.

“My clients can expect only the highest level of service from me and those on my team,” said Juan.

With a commitment to excellence and a deep-seated passion for helping others, he stands ready to tackle even the most challenging cases.

Securing Results for Families Impacted by Mesothelioma

Throughout his career, Juan has recovered significant compensation for mesothelioma patients and their loved ones.

These mesothelioma settlements and verdicts have helped families pay for medical bills, lost wages, everyday living expenses and more.

Find out more about some of his past mesothelioma trial verdicts:

$20 million: A Florida jury awarded Juan’s client compensatory damages after he was exposed to asbestos in joint compound while remodeling an apartment. The lawsuit was filed against Union Carbide, who tried to argue the victim didn’t have mesothelioma. Juan worked with multiple experts to confirm his client’s diagnosis in court.

$14.2 million: Juan represented a contractor who was exposed to asbestos in drywall joint compounds and textured ceiling sprays. He argued that Union Carbide failed to warn the victim about the presence of asbestos in these products, and the Florida Supreme Court ruled in his favor. The company was ordered to pay nearly half of the total damages.

$14 million: In another trial against Union Carbide, Juan represented the daughter of a man who passed away from mesothelioma. The case was retried three times, highlighting Juan’s unwavering commitment to his client. He was ultimately successful in his pursuit of justice on her behalf.

Nearly $13 million: Juan was able to hold Bechtel Corp. accountable after a utility worker got sick from removing asbestos-containing insulation at a power plant. He proved the company, which oversaw maintenance at the plant, had a responsibility to protect workers.

$9 million: After filing a mesothelioma wrongful death lawsuit against Northrop Grumman, Juan secured a significant verdict for the widow of a U.S. Army veteran. The company claimed samples of the victim’s lung tissue didn’t show significant asbestos exposure, but Juan secured test results from the Italian government that proved otherwise.

$3.6 million: A jury ruled in favor of a woman who was exposed to asbestos secondhand while working at Ford Motor Company. Juan discovered internal documents showing the company knew their products were dangerous, despite claiming otherwise in court.

Juan has tried 25 mesothelioma cases to verdict. He is dedicated to holding asbestos companies accountable for their negligence and ensuring that victims receive the justice and compensation they deserve.

Additional Success in the Courtroom

In addition to mesothelioma lawsuits, Juan has successfully represented clients in cases involving employment discrimination, defective product designs and more.

As a skilled negotiator, he has secured individual settlements ranging from $1 million to $29 million.

Additionally, Juan has handled six class action lawsuits, showcasing his ability to manage complex cases and coordinate with multiple plaintiffs.

His experience extends to federal and state appellate courts, where he has briefed and argued numerous cases. Juan has a deep understanding of complex legal principles and is able to persuasively argue nuanced points of law.

“My strengths are decades of honing my craft, perseverance and ‘thinking outside of the box’, explained Juan.

In total, Juan has tried over 50 cases to verdict. His ability to achieve favorable outcomes in both class actions and individual lawsuits has solidified his reputation as a skilled lawyer across various areas of law.

Background & Experience

Juan studied history and political science at Florida State University. Upon graduation, he attended the Florida State University School of Law, where he was the editor-in-chief of the Journal of Land-Use and Environmental Law.

Since 2000, Juan has been a board-certified civil trial lawyer. To achieve this certification, a lawyer must meet rigorous standards that typically include substantial involvement in civil trial law, a high level of peer review, and passing a comprehensive examination.

In his free time, Juan gives back to his community by partaking in numerous ministries within the Archdiocese of Miami. He is also fluent in Spanish.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Daily Business Review, “Most Effective Lawyer in Product Liability Cases”, 2010

AV Preeminent®

attorneys.name: Peter C. Beard
attorneys.practice_type: DUI / Drivers License Reinstatement Lawyers in Springfield, IL
attorneys.bio:
Born in Springfield, Illinois, February 19, 1969. Peter grew up there and went to Springfield High School. Peter’s family roots are deep in Springfield and central Illinois, a heritage that includes a longstanding presence in the legal community. His great, great Grandfather, John C. Lanphier was a lawyer in private practice at Patton & Lanphier, whose own father, Charles H. Lanphier advised Lincoln rival Stephen A. Douglas as well as serving as the Circuit Clerk of Sangamon County. Today, Peter preserves that tradition in the law at Holley, Rosen and Beard serving clients in a wide range of legal affairs throughout central Illinois.

Peter received his Bachelor of Arts in Political Science from Bradley University in Peoria, Illinois in 1992 and his law degree in 1997 from Southern Illinois University in Carbondale, Illinois. He returned to Springfield after law school working as an Assistant States Attorney in the Sangamon County States Attorney's Office, and then as an Assistant Attorney General for the Illinois Attorney General. Thereafter, Peter joined Holley, Rosen & Beard. Peter practices in many areas of law including personal injury, criminal law, DUI/traffic and driver's license reinstatement cases, and general civil litigation. He is licensed in Illinois; also admitted to practice before U.S. District Court, Southern and Central Districts of Illinois, and U.S. Court of Claims/Vaccine Court.

attorneys.name: Leonard S. Becker
attorneys.firm_name: Law Offices of Leonard S. Becker
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury -- Plaintiff Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
Leonard S. Becker is the founder of the Law Offices of Leonard S. Becker, where he focuses on representing individuals who have been injured due to another's negligence.

For the past 18 years, he has worked on behalf of accident victims obtaining full and fair compensation for their injuries, wage losses, and medical expenses. His extensive experience spans representation of clients injured due to wrongful death, bus and car accidents, sidewalk defects, work accidents, and dog attacks.

Mr. Becker's unique combination of compassion and strength has resulted in a proven track record of success on behalf of his clients. Some of his cases, including those involving the CTA, have been featured in various media outlets including the Chicago Tribune, Chicago Sun-Times, Chicago Daily Law Bulletin and Univision.

Based on his experience, Mr. Becker's preferred method of resolution combines strategy and advocacy. His negotiation skills have resulted in many successful outcomes on behalf of his clients. He is also a proven trial attorney and has obtained verdicts for his clients in both state and federal courts.

He is a committed and compassionate advocate and these traits are reflected in his efforts outside of his legal practice. He has been involved as an education volunteer since the mid 1990's. Over the years his volunteerism has included grammar school and adult literacy tutoring. He has served the public schools near his home as a member of the Local School Counsel of two grammar schools and chairing several Parent Teacher Organization committees. Since 1994, he has been a volunteer attorney with Chicago Volunteer Legal Services providing legal representation to those who cannot otherwise afford legal services. He was a past recipient of the organization's Distinguished Service Award.

Mr. Becker is licensed to practice law in the state of Illinois and is admitted to practice before all state courts in Illinois , the Federal District Court for the Northern District of Illinois, and the Seventh Circuit Court of Appeals. He is also a member of the Illinois Bar, Federal Trial Bar for the Northern District of Illinois, and the Illinois Trial Lawyers Association.

Mr. Becker received a B.A. from the University of Illinois at Champaign-Urbana in 1988 and a J.D. from Chicago Kent College of Law in 1992.

Mr. Becker has close ties to the Chicagoland area, he was raised in a suburb of Chicago , attended law school in the city, and continues to live and raise his family here. In addition to spending time with his wife and five children, he enjoys running and has completed over a dozen marathons.

attorneys.name: Jennifer Behme
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in O'Fallon, IL
attorneys.bio:
Jennifer Behme attended University of Illinois at Chicago where she received a Bachelor of Arts with Distinction in Criminal Justice and a minor in psychology before pursuing her Juris Doctorate at St. Louis University School of Law. While there she was involved in the SLU Law Ambassadors program and the SLU Law Mentors programs and received a Certificate in Health Law.

During law school, she had the opportunity to work at Land of Lincoln Legal Assistance Foundation where she assisted indigent clients with Orders of Protection, divorces, real estate matters where she developed an interest in family law.

Since being admitted to the Illinois Bar, Mrs. Behme has practiced throughout Southern Illinois primarily in the area of family law, as well as probate, real estate, and appellate work.

Mrs. Behme has also continued her affiliation with Land of Lincoln assisting indigent individuals through pro bono referral representation. She is the recipient of the Joseph Bartylak Pro Bono Award for her pro bono work and her commitment to the St. Clair County Bar Association Family Law Seminar committee which is coordinated in affiliation with Land of Lincoln Legal Aid each year.

attorneys.name: Luke A. Behme
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in O'Fallon, IL
attorneys.bio:
Luke Behme grew up in Carlinville, Illinois surrounded by small businesses including his mother's accounting firm and his grandfather's farm. He has seen first hand the issues that self-employed and small business owners encounter in the planning stages and the day to day operations of their businesses. Growing up, he was an active member of both 4-H and FFA where he received his American FFA Degree.

At UIUC, he was an active member and officer in organizations such as ACES Student Advancement Committee, ACES Global Ambassadors, and ACES Student Counsel. He graduated with a Bachelor of Science degree in animal sciences and received a Minor in International Agriculture, Consumer and Environmental Sciences.

While at St. Louis University School of Law, he was involved in the SLU Law Ambassadors program and the SLU Law Mentors program. He received a Certificate in International Law along with concentrations in Taxation/Estate Planning and Business Transactions.

While in law school, he interned with the office of the Illinois Attorney General and primarily worked on business compliance and administrative law issues. He also clerked at a small boutique law firm where he gained litigation experience.

Since being admitted to the Illinois Bar, Mr. Behme has practiced throughout Southern Illinois in the areas of family law and general civil litigation. He has also had a substantial appellate practice.

attorneys.name: Jeremy Bell
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
Bell Law was founded in 2005 by Jeremy Bell, a Chicago Kent College of Law graduate, who has been in practice for over five years. Attorney Bell spent his first two years out of law school as a litigator at Quinn, Johnston, Henderson & Pretorius, an insurance defense firm, in Peoria, Illinois. He defended policy holders of various insurers, including State Farm, Allstate and Country Companies. He represented the policy holders in personal injury, premises liability, commercial litigation, defamation, and medical malpractice cases. It was in this capacity that he gained extraordinarily valuable courtroom experience that his peers in Chicago were not yet at a level to enjoy.

After two years as a litigator, Attorney Bell began practicing transactional law at Vonachen, Lawless, Trager & Slevin in Peoria. He gained valuable experience in diverse areas of the law, including real estate, small business/corporate, tax, professional licensure, estate planning and municipal. Among these varied cases he drafted commercial and residential leases; incorporated small business owners (including physicians and dentists); represented an RN who was faced with a narcotics theft charges; drafted wills, trusts and powers of attorney; and prepared tax returns.

In addition to Attorney Bell's formal legal education and training, he is a very experienced negotiator, drawing from his undergraduate education at DePaul University in Chicago. He graduated with honors with a degree in Industrial/Organization Psychology, a field that focuses on developing interpersonal skills, evaluating and adjusting to human behavior and social dynamics. This has provided Attorney Bell with an advantage in his negotiations and, more generally, his practice of law.

Jeremy Bell

Sahara is a dedicated advocate for her clients, with a demonstrated ability to handle complex and demanding family law cases. As a product of divorce parents, she has the utmost empathy for her clients as she advocates vehemently for their needs.

As a recipient of the Trial Advocacy Certificate, she has the ability to gather, evaluate, and analyze information to effectively provide adequate representation. Sahara’s experience as an alternative dispute resolution intern at the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, allows her to utilize her stellar negotiation techniques. Sahara is results-oriented, fearless, and determined to get the best results for her clients.

attorneys.bio:
Charles J. Bellock is a member of the Estate Planning Department, focusing his practice principally in the areas of Wealth Transfer and Estate Planning and Special Needs Planning.

Mr. Bellock has been practicing law in the areas of tax and financial matters, as well as business and estate planning and administration since 1973.

In his free time, Mr. Bellock plays golf as often as possible. He is a past President of Butterfield Country Club in Oak Brook.

He also enjoys spending time with his daughters and grandchildren in Chicago and Boston.

attorneys.name: Sara L. Bendoff
attorneys.firm_name: John J. Malm & Associates Personal Injury Lawyers
attorneys.practice_type: Automobile Accident Liability Lawyers in Naperville, IL
attorneys.bio:
Sara attended Illinois State University where she studied politics and government and philosophy. At Illinois State University, Sara was involved in numerous extra-curricular activities, including The Political Science Club and the Illinois State University Mock Trial Team.

Upon graduation, Sara enrolled in The John Marshall Law School. As a law student, Sara received academic honors, received numerous individual and team awards at mock trial competitions, and served as Associate Barrister of The Trial Advocacy and Alternative Dispute Resolution Honors Executive Board. She also served as an Oral Advocacy Teaching Assistant for Lawyering Skills I.

During law school, Sara worked for a prestigious personal injury law firm in Chicago. Sara obtained first-hand experience in cases involving medical malpractice, and nursing home negligence. These experiences allowed Sara to gain extensive knowledge of personal injury discovery and litigation.

Sara was also an extern for the Honorable Judge Irwin J. Solganick in the Law Division of the Circuit Court of Cook County. There, she was able to observe numerous personal injury trials, analyze pre-trial motions, and gain valuable insight into the world of civil litigation.

In May of 2013, Sara received her Juris Doctorate from the John Marshall School of Law and graduated with a certificate of specialty in Alternative Dispute Resolution.

In 2013, Sara joined John Malm & Associates, P.C. Sara represents individuals and families who have been injured due to the fault of others. Sara is passionate about representing clients who have been victims of medical malpractice and automobile accidents.

Professional Philosophy

Sara is dedicated to achieving a recovery for her clients who have suffered injuries due to the fault of others. Sara understands how important open communication with her clients is to their peace of mind during this difficult time. " If you've been the victim of any kind of injury at someone else's hands, this process can be overwhelming and frightening. It's important my clients understand what steps we take for them and why we do so. Making sure my client's questions are answered always puts them at ease."

Non-Legal Activities

Sara enjoys spending time with her friends and family. In her leisure time, she enjoys trying new restaurants, seeing live music, and reading.

attorneys.name: Valeria Benitez
attorneys.firm_name: The Illinois Hammer Injury Law Firm | Dworkin & Maciariello
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
Valeria Benitez is a seasoned personal injury attorney driven by a profound sense of justice, shaped by her life experiences. She has worked in complex medical malpractice cases as well as multi-district litigation personal injury cases.

With a wealth of experience in workers’ compensation and personal injury law, Valeria embarked on her journey representing victims at a plaintiff’s toxic-tort firm. Witnessing the profound impact of asbestos exposure on blue-collar workers ignited her resolve to be their unwavering voice in the pursuit of justice.

Valeria’s upbringing instilled a deep sense of duty to uplift the underprivileged, a value she actively upholds through community involvement. As the current legal affairs commission chair of a Chicago-based nonprofit, she remains steadfast in her mission to empower others.

Inspired by her father’s commitment to justice in Ecuador, Valeria recalls, “I would hear his interactions with his clients, and I was moved to see how thankful they were when he won their cases, and the way he zealously represented and fought for each of them. I knew I’d want to follow in his footsteps.”

Being fluent in Spanish fosters trust and clarity with Spanish-speaking clients, complementing her relentless advocacy and meticulous organization. Her ties to the Spanish-speaking community are far-reaching, as she also worked in a law firm in Mexico City for several years. She is a persistent go-getter that advocates for her clients. Valeria’s unique blend of legal expertise and genuine empathy makes her a beacon of hope for those navigating personal injury law, offering unwavering support and commitment to their cause.

Married and a devoted mother, she finds solace in family and maintains a vibrant lifestyle as an enthusiastic runner who loves to participate in races, and who has previously competed in martial arts tournaments. While in law school, Valeria learned firsthand about other legal systems and experienced other cultures when she studied abroad in Madrid, Berlin, and Havana. Her compassion extends beyond personal pursuits, reflected in her unwavering dedication to advocating for the rights of the injured in her legal practice.

attorneys.name: Mary Pat Benz
attorneys.firm_name: Mary Patricia Benz, Attorney at Law
attorneys.practice_type: Mediation and Arbitration Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
Mary Patricia Benz, an experienced trial and appellate attorney, opened a solo practice in downtown Chicago concentrating on professional responsibility counseling, litigation, administrative hearings, appeals, and alternative dispute resolution.

Ms. Benz has over 40 years of experience in state and federal courts. She focuses on all types of dispute resolution for individuals and businesses including lawyers, educators, and other professionals. She served for over ten years as a volunteer hearing board member and chair for Attorney Registration and Disciplinary Commission (ARDC).

Ms. Benz was trained as a mediator in the DePaul University College of Law mediation program. She serves as an Arbitrator and Mediator with the American Arbitration Association.

Ms. Benz has been continuously present in Illinois Super Lawyers list of top-rated attorneys since 2005. Only five percent of lawyers in the state are named by Super Lawyers Magazine.

Ms. Benz graduated magna cum laude from Northwestern University School of Law in 1978 where she was selected for the Order of the Coif. While in Law School, she also served as a legal writing instructor. She received her Bachelor of Arts with distinction in psychology from the University of Illinois in Chicago. She is a frequent author and presenter on the topics of mediation, litigation, appeal issues and professional ethics.

Ms. Benz serves as a mediator and arbitrator with the American arbitration Association. The American Arbitration Association has been a leader in cost effective private dispute resolution, resolving nearly 8 million cases since 1926. It is the largest arbitral institution in the world. The ICDR®—International Centre for Dispute Resolution®— is the international division of the American Arbitration Association® (AAA®). The ICDR is the foremost provider of global conflict-resolution solutions to businesses and organizations involved in cross-border disputes.

Ms. Benz has served as an adjunct professor teaching a trial advocacy course at Northwestern University School of Law for 20 years and was an instructor for the National Institute for Trial Advocacy (NITA) Midwest Deposition Program for over 14 years. She also served as an adjunct faculty member at Loyola University of Chicago School of Law teaching trial practice.

Ms. Benz is also active in several bar associations, including the Appellate Lawyers Association, where she served as membership co-chair, and the Chicago Bar Association. She served on the Executive Committee of the Chicago Bar Association’s Judicial Evaluation Committee and as a Board Member of the Association of Attorney-Mediators. She was a volunteer mediator for the Center for Conflict Resolution in the Circuit Court of Cook County Mortgage Foreclosure Mediation Program. She also serves as a mediator in the Circuit Court of Will County Illinois.

Ms. Benz is also the recipient of the Chicago Bar Association, William J. White Award (2004) for service to the Judicial Evaluation Committee for multi-year contribution of time and expertise, and for the vigor and integrity for managing a particularly challenging year as Chair of the Investigation Division. Ms. Benz was recently honored by the ARDC and Supreme Court of Illinois “in recognition and appreciation of substantial contribution to the public, the legal profession and the courts, by serving with distinction as a Member of the Attorney Disciplinary System.”

Previously, Ms. Benz spent ten years as a litigation partner at Winston & Strawn LLP. Prior to that, she was a partner at the Chicago firms of Quinlan & Crisham Ltd. and Phelan Pope & John, Ltd.

attorneys.name: John R. Berg
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
John is a highly experienced trial attorney with well over one hundred jury trials to his credit as well as hundreds of bench trials and arbitrations. He has represented clients in State court throughout Illinois as well as clients in State and Federal Courts from Iowa to New Jersey, and from Wisconsin to Florida. John routinely handles civil cases involving catastrophic injury or death and has obtained multiple judgments of more than a million dollars. John believes that his extensive litigation and trial experience is helpful whether he is resolving disputes inside or outside of court.

The Ford Heights Litigation exemplifies the wide range of John's legal skills. John's client, Paula Gray, had been charged with murder and had served ten years for a crime she did not commit. John tried Paula's post-conviction case and won, clearing Paula of all her charges. This hearing in front of Judge William O'Neill resulted in the longest written decision (352 pages) in Illinois history. The real murderers were charged and convicted. John then filed for and helped her get a pardon for actual innocence from the Governor of Illinois. John also helped Paula recover over $100,000.00 in the Illinois Court of Claims for her wrongful incarceration. John then sued the Cook County Sheriff's Department and forced them to pay Paula $4,000,000.00 for this malicious and unjust prosecution. John then set up an Estate for Paula. Now the Northern Trust Company manages Paula's money and her home expenses, and will pay her bills for the rest of her life.

Recently John had a former client stop in without an appointment. She was very upset as her underage son had been driving while highly intoxicated and been killed in an accident earlier that morning. She was hoping John would be able to retrieve her son's personal belongings from the morgue for her. The son had been overserved by a bar in Miami that led to his fatal accident. John not only personally recovered her son's personal belongings, but also secured a seven figure settlement against the bar that had overserved her son causing his death.

John received his Bachelor of Arts degree at Northwestern University, with honors. He went on to receive his Juris Doctor degree from Hastings College of the Law at the University of California where he served as Senior Managing Editor of the Hastings Communications and Entertainment Law Journal. Following his graduation from law school, John worked with Thomas Decker, one of Chicago's finest trial attorneys. John worked on numerous federal and state trials, successfully litigating issues as varied as race discrimination, Illinois first DNA case, multi-million dollar negligence claims and murder. John then joined the DuPage County State's Attorney's Office as an Assistant State's Attorney where he was known for his strong work ethic and exceptional skill as a courtroom advocate. As an Assistant State's Attorney, John specialized in prosecuting complex financial and violent crimes. John received commendations from various police and community organizations as well as an award from the United States Congress for his work as a prosecutor.

When he was younger, John worked his way through high school, college and law school as a commercial fisherman in the dangerous waters of Alaska. These days, John still enjoys fishing a great deal, but only for sport in the much safer waters off the Florida Keys.

attorneys.name: Peter K. Berg
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
Peter Berg is the founding partner of Berg & Berg with over 30 years of experience in the personal injury field. Peter is a highly skilled and experienced trial lawyer, litigator and negotiator, with over one hundred trials, approximately one thousand arbitrations, as well as millions of dollars every year, in settlements, awards and verdicts in various court houses in and around the Chicago area.

Peter started his law career as an insurance defense attorney, representing people and businesses with insurance, who were accused of injuring others by their wrongful actions in court. The insurance company hires and pays the attorney to represent and defend the alleged wrongdoer in a court action for money damages. Peter had an almost perfect record of success defending his clients in jury trials and obtained more than 30 not guilty verdicts favoring his clients.

In 1997, Peter switched sides and dedicated himself exclusively to representing those who were wronged by others in personal injury and wrongful death cases. The insurance agencies that Peter once defended are the institutions that he fights against on behalf of injured clients. Analyzing a case from a defense perspective as well as a Plaintiff’s perspective helps Peter capitalize on the strengths and weaknesses of a Personal injury or Wrongful Death case, earning Peter a high record of success in winning money damages for his injured clients.

Peter has applied his experience, strength and hope, as well as a knowledge of the law, persistence and hard work, to many different types of accident, wrongful death and injury cases. He has represented injured clients from all walks of life, in accident cases involving:

Motor vehicles, pedestrians, bicycles, motorcycles, trucks, boats and barges

Bus and Public Transportation

Construction accidents

Elevator, escalator & mechanical malfunctions

Fires and explosions

Falls

Medical malpractice

Attacks and injuries caused by Dogs and Animals

Food poisoning

The types of injuries that Peter has litigated include:

Death from drowning, explosions, fire, motor vehicle accidents, food poisoning, murder, drunk driving, falls, medical malpractice

Paralysis

Amputations

Brain injuries

Neck and back injuries

Fractures, tears, scars, and many other traumatic injuries.

Peter received his law degree from De Paul University College of Law in Chicago where he graduated at the top of his class. Peter earned his undergraduate degree in English and Spanish literature from Northwestern University in Evanston, Illinois and also spent one year studying at the University of Sevilla in Seville, Spain. Peter is bilingual in Spanish and English. In his spare time, Peter enjoys the company of his wife, Martha and their four children. He also enjoys cycling, herpetology, camping, hiking, fishing and a good story.

attorneys.practice_type: Automobile Dealerships Lawyers in Arlington Heights, IL
attorneys.bio:
Adam focuses his practice on Corporate, Complex Commercial Litigation, Insurance Defense, and Employment matters. Adam serves as outside general counsel to numerous privately held companies in the Greater Chicago Area, including many automobile dealerships and construction companies. He is regularly engaged to defend lawsuits alleging breach of contract, fraud, breach of warranty, and violations of Federal statutes such as the Truth in Lending Act. Adam is often retained to resolve shareholder disputes and employment charges filed with the EEOC and Illinois Department of Human Rights. Adam also has extensive experience defending construction companies against claims of negligence and wrongful death.

Adam has been recognized as a Super Lawyer Rising Star in Construction Litigation and is the proud recipient of an Illinois Jury Verdict Reporter “Trial Lawyer Excellence Award” for obtaining a defense verdict on behalf of an electrical contractor in a wrongful electrocution death case. Prior to establishing DeVore Radunsky Miller Berger LLC, Adam was a partner in a large, multi-state law firm and the owner of a boutique law firm in Chicago.

attorneys.name: Kristina Berkover
attorneys.practice_type: Complex Litigation Lawyers in Alton, IL
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Kristina Berkover is an associate at Simmons Hanly Conroy in the Complex Litigation Department. She focuses her practice on complex litigation with a specialization in prescription opioid and pharmaceutical cases. Her responsibilities include managing the discovery process and preparing for trial against companies that have caused harm in the opioid epidemic.

"I work with meticulous attention to detail in an effective and efficient way to ensure the best results for our clients," Kristina said. "I truly believe in the work our firm does."

Fighting the Opioid Epidemic

Simmons Hanly Conroy is at the forefront of unprecedented litigation that seeks to resolve the ongoing opioid epidemic. The litigation seeks to secure meaningful funds for communities that incurred millions in costs related to dealing with the estimated 400,000 opioid-related deaths since 1996.

Kristina's primary role involves coordinating with teams of attorneys during the discovery process to ensure each detail of important information gets the attention it deserves. She reviews documents to make sure sensitive information is protected and conveyed to attorneys before they handle a case in court. She also researches and analyzes discovery and varying components of the case, supplying vital information for depositions.

"Each step makes progress in the fight toward justice for those impacted by the opioid epidemic," she said. "Ensuring things are done properly in the discovery process forms the foundation for meaningful results for our clients."

Background and Experience

In addition to Kristina's main practice area of opioid litigation, she has worked on discovery for the DePuy Pinnacle litigation involving patients harmed by Johnson & Johnson's metal-on-metal hip implants as well as document production review on a case involving shattering roofs in Nissan vehicles. She also assisted with the discovery process on lawsuits involving potential vision damage from Elmiron, a prescription medication to treat bladder discomfort associated with interstitial cystitis.

Prior to joining the firm, Kristina advocated for clients in family and immigration law and appeared regularly in state and federal court. She worked with refugees seeking asylum as well as victims of domestic violence. During law school, she worked for multiple Illinois state agencies, developing knowledge of the public sector.

"Before my legal career, I advocated for the public interest in the public, private, and non-profit sectors," Kristina said. "These past experiences bring a unique perspective to the cases I work on at Simmons Hanly Conroy."

Juan C. Bernal is an associate attorney at Lesser Lutrey Pasquesi & Howe, LLP, where he specializes in Trust and Estate litigation, fiduciary litigation, probate administration, and adult guardianships.

Super Lawyers Rising Star: As a 2024 Super Lawyers Illinois Rising Star, Juan represents an elite group of attorneys chosen and rated by their peers for their exceptional skills and commitment to their clients’ best interests. This accolade is a testament to Juan’s standing among his peers as the Rising Stars list celebrates no more than 2.5 percent of attorneys in each state who are in the early stages of their career and under 40 years old.

Legal Experience: Juan’s legal career is marked by dedication and excellence. Before joining Lesser Lutrey Pasquesi & Howe, LLP, Juan honed his skills in legal advocacy and litigation by representing individuals and businesses in commercial disputes, corporate breach of fiduciary duty actions, and civil rights matters. Juan also clerked for judges in both state and federal courts. This experience equipped him with a deep understanding of various facets of the law and legal procedure, and a keen insight into navigating complex legal issues.

Passions Beyond the Law: Beyond his legal career, Juan was a teaching assistant and instructor at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, where he taught philosophy and advanced composition. In his leisure time, Juan is an avid soccer player and enjoys reading political and legal philosophy.

Multilingual and Multicultural: Juan was born in Bogota, Colombia, and is fluent in Spanish (Se Habla Español). His multicultural background provides a unique perspective and enriches his ability to serve a diverse range of clients.

attorneys.name: Steven A. Berman
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Litigation Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
Steve Berman has over 30 years of experience in the area of personal injury litigation, including trying, as first chair attorney, over 60 personal injury jury trials throughout the state of Illinois, including Cook, DuPage, DeKalb, Federal District Court Northern District of Illinois, Lake, LaSalle, McHenry, McLean, Winnebago, and Whiteside counties. Three of these trials resulted in jury verdicts in excess of insurance policy limits when insurers had refused to settle prior to trial. With Anesi Ozmon, Ltd. since 1998, he has also briefed and argued before the First, Second, and Third District, Illinois Appellate Courts.

Steve has successfully appeared before the Appellate Court in the state of Illinois in a significant case upholding the rights of all injured victims who slip and fall on ice. In the case Russell v. the Village of Lake Villa, the trial court dismissed the Plaintiff’s case because it found that the Plaintiff’s injury was caused by ice that was considered to be a natural accumulation under previous case law. Steve appealed and the Appellate Court reversed and found that where unsafe plowing procedures cause ice to form, that ice is not a natural accumulation, and a successful settlement was obtained. In addition, Steve successfully argued that the trial court was wrong to dismiss a construction negligence case where the proof established that the General Contractor controlled safety on the job site. In the case Foley v. Builtech Construction Inc., the Appellate Court reversed and remanded the case. A successful settlement was ultimately achieved.

“I believe that all of my clients deserve to be treated with respect and professionalism at all times. Each client’s injury is unique to him or her and I will do whatever it takes to obtain the maximum compensation possible on their behalf.”

Steve is a dedicated litigator who stops at nothing to achieve success and significant awards for his clients. He has been consistently named as one of the Leading Lawyers in Illinois for personal injury attorneys. In addition, Steve has given presentation lectures to members of ITLA (Illinois Trial Lawyers Association), and has served as a member of the Board of managers of ITLA.

Steve has achieved over $90 million in compensation for his clients. Some notable results include:

Construction Negligence:

$10.03 million settlement for a union ironworker who sustained serious knee and wrist injuries requiring multiple surgeries when, while erecting industrial racking at a large warehouse in Aurora, a row of racks was caused to tip and fall over onto his man lift. The defendants responsible for the construction site offered $4.5 million to settle prior to trial which was rejected. However, after 5 days of trial in Federal Court, the settlement was achieved.

$5.3 million settlement for a 40-year-old Local 1 Ironworker who sustained a herniated disk while installing rebar on a construction site in Chicago. The injury required three surgeries including a fusion of the L5-S1 disk space in the lumbar spine as well as follow up pain management care.

$3.5 million settlement for a 58-year-old Local 1 Ironworker who was injured while going to work on a high-rise renovation project in Chicago when the freight elevator he was in fell two stories from the ground level to the sub-basement level due to being overloaded. The ironworker sustained neck and back injuries which required spinal fusion surgery as well as needing a spinal cord stimulator implanted for pain management.

$2.5 million jury verdict for a union electrician IBEW Local 134 who injured his knee requiring arthroscopic surgery after he twisted his knee coming down from a ladder while working at a UPS packaging facility, when the UPS package cart bumped into his ladder. The Defendant offered $125,000 prior to trial to settle the case which was rejected.

$2.25 million total package settlement for union laborer Local 1035 who was injured during a tunneling project when rocks and slag fell onto him, cracking his hard hat and injuring his neck.

$2.1 million in total package settlement for a 50-year-old union ironworker Local 393 who fell approximately 14 feet after slipping and losing his balance while walking on open steel beams, landing on the concrete floor below. He sustained fractures to both wrists as well as a ruptured spleen requiring emergency surgery. The worker was not provided with or using fall protection at the time of the injury.

$1.9 million total package settlement for a union iron worker Local 444 who slipped on unsafe ground conditions on a construction site in Putnam County suffering a herniated disc and requiring discectomy surgery and pain management.

$1.7 million total package settlement for a union ironworker Local 465 who injured his back in a slip and fall while working to secure metal decking on a steel roof at a jobsite in Vermillion County.

$1.52 million settlement for a Local 393 iron worker who was caused to trip and fall due to hole that should have been backfilled on a construction site in Batavia. Our client sustained a torn rotator cuff requiring surgical repair.

$1.5 total package settlement for a union ironworker who injured his shoulder while manually installing angle iron from a man lift.

$1.5 million total package settlement for a union painter who injured his knee while climbing an old wooden affixed ladder on a jobsite in Chicago.

$1.5 million settlement for a Local 152 Laborer who injured his ring finger when washing out a concrete bucket. The fracture got infected and failed to properly heal and the last joint on the ring finger needed to be permanently fused.

$9.0 Million settlement for the electrocution death of a minor in an industrial accident in Central Illinois. The incident was unwitnessed and the Defendants claimed that they were not aware of or responsible for any unsafe condition that caused the death. The settlement was reached after extensive discovery had been completed. The deceased minor left behind his parents and a brother. The parties to the settlement are confidential.

$6.624 million jury verdict for a Local 498 Ironworker who injured his back when he tripped and fell on a job site in Belvidere, IL. The Ironworker sustained a L4-5 herniated disc requiring laminectomy surgery and impacting his ability to continue working in a heavy profession. The defense offered $250,000 to settle prior to trial, which was rejected.

$4.55 million settlement for a 57-year-old union caulker who was working out of a large boom lift that was stuck by a passing box truck while he was working outside the building under construction in Chicago. He was caused chest trauma and multiple right rib fractures, a collapsed lung (pneumothorax), and head trauma/concussion. In addition, during his rehabilitation from his injuries, he suffered a herniated disc in his low back that was treated by injections.

$2.25 million settlement for a union electrician who slipped and fell on a sheet of ice in a warehouse under construction. The ice accumulated as a result of the general contractor’s failure to block the open doors and windows that had not yet been installed when it should have know that an over-night snow storm was on the way. Our client sustained a right shoulder rotator cuff tear and meniscus tear in his knee requiring surgery.

Slip and Fall / Motor Vehicle:

$4.55 million settlement for motorcycle crash causing severe TBI and requiring emergency life saving brain surgery. Our client a 55 year old man self-employed in trucking was caused to crash his motorcycle due to unsafe road paving (resurfacing) work performed on a busy road in Chicago.

$2.55 million settlement for a man working as a “flagman” when a large truck rolled over his lower leg causing the leg to be amputated.

$1.75 million settlement for a student who had suffered a severe concussion when an inflatable amusement ride malfunctioned at a post-high school prom event. Our client was struck in the head with a chain when the apparatus came apart, and he continues to suffer from migraine headaches as a result of his head injury.

$950,000 settlement for a semi-truck driver who was rear-ended by another truck while in traffic on I-80. He sustained a herniated disc which required surgery and continuing chiropractic care.

$668,750 settlement for pedestrians who were struck while crossing Aurora Avenue in Naperville by a Naperville Police Officer. The Village of Naperville argued that it was immune from suit under the law. It filed multiple motions to dismiss which were defeated.

$440,000 settlement for a union ironworker apprentice Local 63 who injured her back requiring an IDET procedure when she slipped and fell on water on the floor at a Jewel food store in DuPage County.

$437,000 total package settlement for a union painter who suffered a torn rotator cuff of his shoulder in a fall from an improperly placed ladder on a job site.

$2.8575 million record jury verdict in Rock Island County on behalf of a Local 111 Ironworker as a result of a motorcycle accident at an intersection. Our client suffered a fractured tibia and fibula requiring surgery. The defendants refused to offer a reasonable settlement. At trial, the defendants denied fault for the accident and blamed our client for improperly operating his motorcycle, which the jury rejected. The damages the jury awarded our client was a record verdict in Rock Island County.$2.3 million settlement for a 47-year-old ironworker who slipped and fell on ice and fractured his right ankle, requiring surgery, during the construction of a wind farm being erected on a large plot of land previously used as farmland. Although the defendant argued that the ice was simply due to the natural weather conditions at the time, we were able to prove that the excavation subcontractor was the cause due to its negligently performed site preparation and excavation work.

attorneys.firm_name: Law Offices of Janice L. Berman
attorneys.practice_type: Adoption Lawyers in Niles, IL
attorneys.bio:
At the Law Offices of Janice L. Berman, we believe in the old-fashioned ideas of returning our clients' phone calls and in being available to help them when they have questions or concerns. We also happen to think that the meter shouldn't start running every time your attorney picks up the phone.

Our law office is located in a former storefront and provides our clients with not just a comfortable and inviting environment in which to meet with their attorney, but also with the ease of accessibility that the 42nd Floor of the John Hancock Building just can't.

Our practice is focused on providing high legal services to individuals and families in Chicago and throughout the suburbs and to helping them to find real life solutions to problems in these areas.

We start working to find those solutions by providing honest evaluations.

This approach works.

Realistic expectations and goals are often followed by real solutions and real solutions produce satisfied clients. The majority of our business is built on referrals of clients who have been pleased by our approach and the results that we provide.

attorneys.name: Frank J. Bertuca
attorneys.firm_name: Katz, Friedman, Eisenstein, Johnson, Bareck & Bertuca
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
Frank J. Bertuca is an aggressive litigator with numerous trial and appellate victories on behalf of his clients. Frank joined Katz Friedman as a workers' compensation attorney in 1999. He proudly represents injured workers in the airline, automotive manufacturing, construction, law enforcement and fire protection industries. Frank also speaks to unions and professional organizations on the subject of work injuries. Prior to joining Katz Friedman, he practiced work injury law and pension litigation for several years.

Frank developed an interest in litigation and ethical standards early in his career. As an undergraduate student, he was privileged to clerk for the Honorable Ronald Dozier in McClean County Circuit Court, where he assisted in divorce and personal injury cases. He also worked on general civil law cases as a clerk for the Honorable James Knecht in the 4th District Appellate Court of Illinois. In 1991, he earned his Juris Doctorate from the Chicago-Kent College of Law, Illinois Institute of Technology where he was a member of Moot Court Society. As an undergraduate, he studied economics and graduated cum laude in 1988 from Illinois State University, where he was a founding member of the university's trial advocacy team. Frank is a member of the Chicago Bar Association, the Illinois State Bar Association, and the Workers' Compensation Lawyers Association.

attorneys.name: Olga Beznashchuk
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
Olga Beznashchuk was born in Ukraine and came to the United States with her family at sixteen. Starting a new life in a country taught Olga to be persistent and never to give up. Olga’s persistence and dedication allowed her to graduate with honors from one of Chicago’s high schools and receive acceptance offers to multiple Illinois universities.

Olga obtained her undergraduate degree from DePaul University with a Political Science major and a Business Administration minor. While studying at the university, Olga conducted volunteer work in underserved communities. Olga helped students from Chicago schools obtain funding for college education by assisting in filling out FAFSA applications and securing scholarships. Olga also volunteered as an aid in Chicago Public Schools on the city’s south side and assisted low-income parents who temporarily lost custody of their children.

Promoting justice for people who do not know their legal rights or do not have access to much-needed legal services is a passion for Olga, and this was one of the main reasons Olga decided to pursue a career in law.

Olga obtained her law degree at Northern Illinois University College of Law and graduated with honors. Now, Olga represents clients from Chicago and the surrounding areas in workers’ compensation and personal injury cases.

Olga Beznashchuk is a member of the Chicago Bar Association and Illinois State Bar Association. Olga is also a member of the ISBA Workers’ Compensation Section Council. Olga is fluent in English, Ukrainian, and Russian and is thrilled to work in the city where she grew up advocating for the injured workers and people hurt due to the negligence of others.

attorneys.name: Nicholas Bigoness
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Moline, IL
attorneys.bio:
Nic comes to the VLAW team with 35 years of experience helping Chicagoland clients navigate the legal system.

Over the last 3+ decades, he has worked primarily on behalf of individuals who’ve been injured by auto accidents, construction accidents, medical negligence, and premises liability issues.

He is experienced in both personal injury and worker’s compensation; and is familiar with the legal process in most Northern Illinois court districts.

Having spent some time handling cases on the defense side for several large, self-insured corporations in regard to liability and workers’ compensation claims, he brings a unique perspective to the VLAW firm that will surely help our clients when entering the negotiation process.

He is very much looking forward to working on the side of “the people” and is committed to holding insurance companies & corporations accountable for the injuries our clients sustain and seeking the recovery they deserve.

Nic is a lifelong resident of the Chicagoland area, having graduated from The John Marshall Law School. He lives in Brookfield. When he’s not fighting for the rights of the injured in Illinois, you can likely find him running, traveling, improving his golf game, or watching his beloved White Sox.
