attorneys.name: Mark P. Standa
attorneys.practice_type: Professional Liability Law Lawyers in Lake Forest, IL
attorneys.bio:
Resume & Biographical History of Mark Standa

Mark is a former equity partner, shareholder, Officer, and Director of the large Chicago law firm of Pretzel & Stouffer, Chartered where, from 1987 to 2002, he concentrated his practice of law in defense litigation, principally in the areas of professional liability, products liability, and construction accident claims. Before going into private practice at Pretzel & Stouffer, Mark was a Cook County, Illinois Assistant States Attorney, where he worked in the Civil Actions Bureau, Federal Litigation Division, defending the County and its employees in Section 1983 civil rights litigation. Over the years, Mark has successfully tried cases to verdict in both jury and bench trials, in both state and federal court, defending his clients in medical malpractice, products liability, premises liability, vehicular liability, Realtor E&O, civil rights, and construction accident cases.

First, as an Assistant States Attorney fresh out of law school, Mark tried civil rights cases in Federal Court. Since entering private practice in 1987, he has litigated, mediated, arbitrated, and tried hundreds of professional liability cases involving medical, legal, realtor, accountant, and insurance broker's malpractice He has similarly handled various other types of defense litigation in the areas of products liability, construction accidents, premises liability, and vehicular liability.

Over the course of the last 25 years, much of Mark's litigation practice has been devoted to the defense of medical professionals, medical institutions, and medical devices/products. He has defended scores of doctors in the fields of psychiatry, orthopedics, OB-GYN, internal medicine, pediatrics, neonatology, oncology, neurology, radiology, anesthesiology, emergency medicine, and cardiology. He has also defended nurses, physical therapists, CNAs, LPNs, a cytotechnologist, and other allied healthcare providers. In addition, he has also developed a particular expertise in defending nursing homes, HMOs, and hospitals as well as the employees of these institutions. Regarding medical devices and other medical products, Mark's litigation experience includes the defense of medicines and their makers, blood products, and spinal fusion devices. Hence, for personal injury cases stemming from many varied causes, Mark has substantial human anatomy experience in virtually all areas of human anatomy especially brain injury claims and associated intangible psychological injury claims such as post-traumatic stress disorder, depression, etc.

In defense of product designers, manufacturers, suppliers and distributors, Mark's comprehensive litigation experience in numerous lawsuits encompasses medical devices, medicines, punch presses, power tools, hand tools, propane gas tanks, trenching/digging machines, conveyor belt systems, amusement park rides, motorcycle wheels, and seating products in both sports stadiums and vehicles. Whether the plaintiff's theory of recovery sounds in warranty, negligence, and/or strict products liability for an alleged unreasonably dangerous product or alleged failure to warn of such danger, Mark has extensively litigated all such theories. Whatever the widget and whatever the injury, Mark's vast experience in products liability litigation, coupled with his experience in medical injury litigation and other personal injury cases, serves as a broad and solid foundation for him to ably defend the accused in this field of law.

In the building/construction field, Mark has extensive litigation experience from cases he has managed and tried concerning various construction accidents and injuries to construction workers, as well as mechanic's lien litigation. He has defended general contractors, subcontractors of all tiers and of all kinds, steel erection companies, demolition companies, and excavating companies.

In the field of real estate law, Mark has broad experience defending Realtors and real estate companies in professional liability or E&O malpractice cases bought by disgruntled house buyers. His experience in this regard encompasses the defense of claims under the Illinois Real Estate License Act, the Illinois Consumer Fraud and Deceptive Practices Act, and common law claims of negligent misrepresentation and fraud. Mark has also successfully represented Plaintiff house buyers against a Realtor and large real estate brokerage company proving violations of the Consumer Fraud Act and the Illinois Real Estate License Act based upon the fact that a house advertised as Brand New had sustained flood water damage, which the Realtor knew about but failed to disclose.

In vehicle liability litigation, Mark's wide-ranging experience is comprehensive. Mark has defended automobile drivers, bus drivers, truck drivers, cab driver, ambulance drivers, medivan drivers, police officers in high-speed pursuit cases, as well as other drivers and their companies.

attorneys.name: Lawrence S. Starkopf
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Offices of Jeffery M. Leving, Ltd.
attorneys.practice_type: Matrimonial Law Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
Lawrence S. Starkopf earned his Juris Doctorate degree from the University of Baltimore School of Law. After graduation he was admitted to the Illinois State Bar, Supreme Court of Illinois and the Federal Bar in 1975. He began his legal career in the Cook County Public Defender’s Office at the Juvenile Detention Center, where he represented and defended juvenile offenders and children who were neglected, abused and abandoned. A significant number of these children came from fatherless homes. After leaving the Public Defender’s Office he began a career in Matrimonial Law and has continued to do so for the last 50 years. Lawrence has litigated many complex and significant cases that impacted the evolution of matrimonial law in the State of Illinois. A few examples of his cases that defined the practice of matrimonial law are set forth below.

He litigated the trial and the appeal to the Supreme Court of Illinois, one of the first cases that defined how the court distinguishes between marital and non-marital assets, with the issues of contribution, dissipation, transmutation and valuation.

He litigated the trial and the Appellate Court appeal of one of the first cases that led to creating the procedure for the valuation of businesses as well as the factors to be considered in such evaluations

He litigated the trial and the Illinois Supreme Court appeal of the first case that set the standard that payment of college expenses are child support and therefore, are limited to contribution to college expenses to be incurred in the future and reimbursement for past expenses incurred cannot be sought.

He litigated the trial and Illinois Supreme Court appeal of one of the first cases that helped set the factors a court is to consider in seeking a bifurcated Judgment for Dissolution of Marriage.

Mr. Starkopf has lectured on matrimonial law, and is a member of the Chicago Bar Association, the Illinois State Bar Association, and is a Leading Matrimonial Lawyer.

Ben graduated from New Athens High School and attended Eastern Illinois University where he graduated with high honors. He continued his education at Southern Illinois University School of Law where he graduated in 2005. Since graduating from Law school, he has concentrated his practice in Central and Southern Illinois and the Metro East. He began clerking with Patrick in 2001 and became a licensed attorney at the firm in 2006.

Ben currently resides in Troy, Illinois, with his wife Keely and their dog Brooklyn. He is a member of the Madison County and St. Clair County Bar Associations. He enjoys crossfit and many recreational activities, including running and golf and is an avid follower all St. Louis sports teams. His father is a retired Mobile Equipment Operator for Headwater Resource and previously worked 13 years for Granite City Steel, and 24 years as a coal miner for Peabody. His mother is a retired registered nurse from Belleville Memorial Hospital, where she worked for over 33 years.

attorneys.name: Mike Stillman
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
Mike Stillman is a veteran attorney with varied practice and significant trial experience. He has tried numerous civil trials to verdict including wrongful death, serious personal injury cases, and class action matters. His experience includes significant party, witness, medical and expert depositions.

Mike was the managing shareholder of a Chicago mid-sized civil practice firm where he was the chair of the trial committee analyzing cases that likely were to go to verdict. He also is general counsel of multiple municipalities and Illinois governmental entities in which he oversees all facets of their legal work including for some, evaluation of exposure in litigated matters. Additionally, he is also a well-recognized practitioner of zoning and development law and related real estate matters with a focus in utilizing economic development and redevelopment tools to result in new facilities.

Mike has been an adjunct professor in various law topics at Lewis University and South Suburban College in Illinois. He is the father of 2 adult children. Mike is the President of Brother Rice High School (Chicago) Foundation and is the Secretary of This Iowa Ballpark, an organization which is responsible for overseeing the ballpark where the Major League game is played at the Field of Dreams Movie Site. When not practicing law, Mike likes to golf and is an avid and sometimes suffering fan of the Chicago White Sox.

attorneys.name: Jay B. Strayer
attorneys.practice_type: Business Services Lawyers in Wheaton, IL
attorneys.bio:
Jay B. Strayer focuses his legal practice on corporate and commercial law, with an emphasis on mergers and acquisitions. Jay also counsels individuals and business owners in their estate planning, probate, and commercial real estate transactional needs.

Jay was a principal in the law firm of Fewkes Wentz & Strayer in Naperville, Illinois until his firm merged with Huck Bouma in 2007. Prior to entering the private practice of law, Jay was Assistant General Counsel of McGraw-Edison Company, where he directed the activities of the corporate legal staff. Jay was also General Counsel and Secretary of Atcor, Inc., a publicly traded manufacturer and distributor of steel conduit pipe and related products. Jay was also Vice President, General Counsel and Secretary of The Jepson Corporation, a diversified holding company that operated ten manufacturing subsidiaries.

Jay is a retired U.S. Naval Reserve Officer (Commander), specializing in defense logistics and contract administration, and served as Commanding Officer of two Naval Reserve Units. He has served his community as a trustee of the Village of Glen Ellyn from 1998-2003, and currently is Vice Chair of the Plan Commission. Jay and his family are longtime residents of Glen Ellyn.

Beginning in 2020, Jay has been appointed to a four year term on the Board of Governors of the University of Kansas Law School.

attorneys.name: William J. Strons
attorneys.practice_type: Business Services Lawyers in Wheaton, IL
attorneys.bio:
William J. Strons joined Huck Bouma, PC in 2002 and has served as the Firm's Managing Shareholder since 2012. Bill also currently serves as Co-Chair of Huck Bouma's M&A and Corporate Transactional practice groups.

With over 25 years of experience in mergers and acquisitions, Bill uses this wealth of knowledge to efficiently evaluate complex business transactions in a manner best suited for the client. Bill has extensive experience in working with both buyers and sellers from various industries in the structuring, implementation, and financing of transactions. In this capacity, Bill has aided clients in:

Designing and implementing strategies

Drafting and reviewing Letters of Intent

Structuring, negotiating, and managing business transactions

Counseling on the tax structure of raising capital

Drafting and reviewing buy-sell agreements

Over the course of his practice, Bill has assisted clients with complex asset and stock acquisitions and divestitures, tax-free reorganizations and restructuring, joint venture agreements, tax-deferred equity rollover transactions, and private placement offerings.

Bill also represents a variety of closely-held businesses in all aspects of their corporate and tax planning matters. With a strong tax background, Bill advises clients on succession planning, federal and state tax planning, compliance, governance, and employment contracts.

Bill is a frequent speaker for a variety of industry organizations, including the Midwest Business Brokers & Intermediaries group, the DuPage Bar Association and the University of Chicago Booth School of Business Entrepreneurial Roundtable. Bill is a past chair of the DuPage Bar Association's Tax Law Committee and has presented topics such as tax strategies in selling the closely-held business, legal due diligence in the M&A transaction, and key terms of a letter of intent.

Bill lives in Naperville with his wife. He is a Chicago sports enthusiast and also enjoys golfing and fishing.

I started my career representing injured workers and accident victims. I love performing extraordinary legal work for extraordinary working people and helping folks of all walks of life. When I started Strong Law Offices in 1999, I wanted a firm that prides itself in being "working lawyers for working people." I have dedicated myself to creating a legal team that is dedicated, hardworking and driven to succeed in life, work and happiness.

I have tried, argued and arbitrated claims and cases from the smallest of towns to the largest of cities. I have received recoveries for employees from all professions, trades and jobs. I have dealt with injuries ranging from catastrophic, complex and complete to minor, major and massive. I have worked and dealt with health care providers, experts, defense attorneys, large companies, insurance carriers and all other obstacles or road blocks placed by opposing parties or carriers to interfere, infringe or infuriate the rights of injured workers or accident victims. I have lobbied for new laws and defended good laws from the efforts of insurance carriers and large business interests to defeat the rights of the poor, the tired and the weak. My life and my law practice are dedicated to the service of helping injured workers and accident victims and will utilize any legal means necessary to protect and preserve those victims' rights to get help and get better from their injury.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
I started my career representing injured workers and accident victims. I love performing extraordinary legal work for extraordinary working people and helping folks of all walks of life. When I started Strong Law Offices in 1999, I wanted a firm that prides itself in being "working lawyers for working people." I have dedicated myself to creating a legal team that is dedicated, hardworking and driven to succeed in life, work and happiness.

I have tried, argued and arbitrated claims and cases from the smallest of towns to the largest of cities. I have received recoveries for employees from all professions, trades and jobs. I have dealt with injuries ranging from catastrophic, complex and complete to minor, major and massive. I have worked and dealt with health care providers, experts, defense attorneys, large companies, insurance carriers and all other obstacles or road blocks placed by opposing parties or carriers to interfere, infringe or infuriate the rights of injured workers or accident victims. I have lobbied for new laws and defended good laws from the efforts of insurance carriers and large business interests to defeat the rights of the poor, the tired and the weak. My life and my law practice are dedicated to the service of helping injured workers and accident victims and will utilize any legal means necessary to protect and preserve those victims' rights to get help and get better from their injury.

attorneys.name: Patrick S. Sullivan
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Frankfort, IL
attorneys.bio:
Patrick S. Sullivan grew up on the Southwest Side of Chicago in Oak Lawn and attended Marist High School in Chicago, Illinois. He graduated magna cum laude from Eastern Illinois with an undergraduate degree in political science. Shortly thereafter he obtained his Juris Doctor from IIT Chicago-Kent College of Law. Prior to actively practicing in the legal field, Patrick served as an escrow closer for Ticor Title Insurance Company where he gained valuable knowledge of all aspects of real estate transactions. Prior to joining Frankfort Law Group, Patrick worked as an associate at another local law firm developing his skills in estate planning, probate and trust administration, estate mediation, guardianship, elder law issues, real estate law, and corporate law.

Patrick has assisted numerous clients in creating Last Wills & Testaments, Revocable and Irrevocable Living Trusts, Life Insurance Trusts, Special Needs Trusts, Honorary Pet Trusts, Powers of Attorney for both Health Care and Property, and Living Wills. He strongly believes in educating his clients on the need and use of proper estate planning. It is his goal as an attorney to build strong relationships and trust with each of his clients in order to achieve the best possible results.

He has also handled a number of complicated decedent's estate and guardianship matters. Often times when a family loses a loved one or is dealing with a member who has a disability there are many questions and concerns that arise. Patrick prides himself in not only helping address the complicated legal issues, but helping cope with some of the more personal matters.

Patrick played college soccer and baseball at both the Junior College and Division 1 levels. He also served as an Assistant Varsity Coach to the Boys Soccer Team at Marist High School while attending law school, and was instrumental in winning two sectional titles. He was also named by Tom Bonen of the Daily Southtown as one of the top 100 influences over the last century on soccer in the southern suburbs.

Patrick is married and is the father to two wonderful girls. They enjoy vacationing in Southern Michigan during the Summer months.

attorneys.name: Stephen Sutera
attorneys.practice_type: Wealth Transfer and Estate Planning Lawyers in Wheaton, IL
attorneys.bio:
Stephen M. Sutera serves in an Of Counsel position in Huck Bouma's Trusts and Estates Practice Group. Since 1990, Stephen has focused his practice on designing estate plans, settling estates, providing advice regarding elder law, and providing advice regarding special needs planning.

He began his career as a Cook County Prosecutor in the Criminal Division. Since beginning his Estate Planning Practice in 1990 he has taught classes to financial planners and accountants regarding Estate Planning, Elder Law Planning, and Wealth Transfer. Stephen has made regular presentations on behalf of Religious Organizations, Retirement Communities, Public Libraries, and other charities dealing with Life Care Planning.

He takes great pride in creating estate planning options, along with implementation of designs. Stephen is committed to client education in order to provide superior service. Stephen creates his planning in an environment which allows each client the opportunity to tell their life story regarding themselves and their family. Thereafter, the clients participate in an educational process of choosing options which will cover their lifetime and beyond. Stephen enjoys collaborating with the client's team of professionals such as their financial planner, tax preparer, and insurance professional.

Stephen brings to Huck Bouma P.C. 33 years of experience from his long career operating his own practice.

Stephen continues to serve on boards of various charities. He resides in Orland Park, IL with Gail, his wife of 41 years.

Stephen is the proud father of two adult daughters, Marissa and Kristen.

Stephen enjoys gardening in his free time.

Honors

Chicago Magazine (November 2015): named as one of the Top Five Star Accounting and Estate Planning Professionals in Chicago.

attorneys.name: Hannah K. Sweeney
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
Hannah Sweeney joined Pavich Law Group, P.C. nearly a decade ago. Prior to becoming an attorney, she worked at PLG as a paralegal while earning her juris doctor at Loyola University Chicago School of Law, where she graduated cum laude. As Hannah has developed her career, specializing in medical malpractice, wrongful death, and personal/catastrophic injury, she has devoted herself to thorough, complex, and thoughtful evaluation of her clients' medical treatments, consultations, procedures, and diagnoses. The connections between medicine and the law are crucial to building her multifaceted practice from initial assessment all the way through aggressive litigation.

Hannah works in tandem with her mentor and PLG managing partner, Anastasia Pavich, to commit the full resources of the firm to every case accepted. She has dedicated her career as a trial attorney to protecting, advocating, and representing those who have suffered from another's negligence. Hannah brings a combination of empathy and personalized attention to detail to her work, and utilizes her crucial understanding of the complexity of the medical, legal, and insurance systems. She also works directly with PLG staff physicians and consulting experts to review, analyze, and interpret medical records and facts to determine how best to prosecute claims. Hannah believes that carefully and respectfully building relationships with clients allows her to be a potent advocate and fosters the trust needed to achieve success on their behalf. This advocacy, facilitated through personal connections with her clients, is the most gratifying element of her profession.

In addition to her Juris Doctor degree and Certificate in Advocacy from Loyola University School of Law, Hannah holds a Certificate of Mediation and has successfully mediated numerous cases, understanding that positions and motives are crucial to reaching settlement outside of trial. Hannah is licensed and admitted to practice in Illinois and Indiana and maintains many memberships in professional and civic organizations, including the American, Illinois, and Chicago Bar Associations; the Illinois Trial Lawyers Association; the American Association for Justice; the Indiana State Bar Association; and the Indiana Trial Lawyers Association.

attorneys.name: Bruno W. Tabis Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Business Services Lawyers in Wheaton, IL
attorneys.bio:
Bruno W. Tabis, Jr. joined Huck Bouma in 2018, after previously practicing in Chicago for nearly 40 years. Bruno serves as general counsel for closely held businesses, concentrating on the formation and maintenance of corporations and LLCs, mergers and acquisitions, employment matters, contract negotiations and UCC issues, as well as consulting and advising the principals on general business matters.

His commercial real estate practice includes purchases and sales, condominium development and conversions, project development and construction contracting, leasing, property management and environmental compliance, permitting and remediation.

Bruno counsels business owners and individuals on estate and succession planning, preparation of Wills, Trusts, and Powers of Attorney, and is experienced in probate proceedings and trust and estate management and administration.

He also practices in the areas of financial institutions and finance, representing both banks and borrowers in loan documentation, mortgage and real estate financing, UCC financing, workouts, forbearances, renegotiations and commercial short sales.

Currently residing in the Stonebridge area of Aurora, Bruno had lived in Wheaton for 35 years, where he continues to be active in the community. He was a founding member and on the original board of directors for the New 200 Foundation and was a long-time member of St. Paul Lutheran Church where he served as President. His wife, Stacie Pierce, teaches English at Wheaton-Warrenville South High School.

Bruno has been rated AV "Preeminent"by Martindale-Hubbell and named to Chicago's Top Rated Lawyers.

Bruno is an accomplished technical, deep wreck SCUBA diver. He has explored numerous Lake Michigan shipwrecks, including the 370 foot deep Carl D. Bradley, a Great Lakes freighter and Edmund Fitzgerald look-alike which also broke up in a November storm.

attorneys.name: Michael R. Taege
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
Michael Taege, the Principal Partner of Taege Law Offices, exemplifies the traits of an effective leader and a brilliant legal tactician. As the cornerstone of the firm, he demonstrates calculated and strategic decision-making that informs his entire approach to litigation. His persevering spirit and tenacious pursuit of justice are the foundation of his esteemed reputation in the Chicago legal community.

Adept at negotiation, Michael leverages his keen analytical skills to advocate effectively on behalf of his clients. His extensive litigation experience, coupled with a results-driven approach, ensures each client is equipped with a robust, tailored strategy designed to secure favorable outcomes. His steely resolve and unwavering commitment become palpable in the courtroom, where he showcases his skill as a proven litigator.

The success of Taege Law Offices is testament to Michael's leadership capabilities. Since establishing the firm, he has transformed it into one of Chicago's premier family law boutiques. This impressive achievement demonstrates not just his profound legal acumen, but also his capacity to motivate and inspire a team of equally dedicated professionals.

Michael's prowess in complex litigation arises from a foundation of invaluable experience. Early in his career, he had the privilege of learning under one of Chicago's top trial litigators, absorbing crucial insights and honing his skills to an exceptional level. This substantial and comprehensive trial experience now informs his approach to every case he takes on.

Yet, at the heart of Michael's practice is an unwavering commitment to providing quality representation to his clients. He is cognizant of the emotional and personal complexities inherent to family law and is dedicated to ensuring each client feels seen, heard, and supported. His aim is to mitigate stress for clients during these challenging times, providing them with peace of mind and confidence in their legal strategy.

Michael Taege's reputation as a preeminent family law attorney does not rest solely on his extensive legal capabilities. It is the confluence of his leadership, perseverance, and relentless pursuit of excellence that sets him apart. His strategic mind, coupled with his unyielding determination, has crafted a law firm that champions client success, ensuring Taege Law Offices stands as a beacon of quality and dedication in the realm of family law.

Amir R. Tahmassebi is currently a partner at Konicek & Dillon and concentrates his practice in the areas of professional negligence, legal ethics, commercial litigation, casualty and sports law. He has successfully defended and prosecuted numerous lawyers, accountants, architects and engineers throughout the nation and has tried dozens of cases to verdict. Mr. Tahmassebi has successfully handled legal malpractice cases on a wide range of issues and recently obtained a defense verdict in a legal malpractice case seeking over ten million in damages. He has represented attorneys, accountants and other professionals in civil and administrative hearings before the Attorney Disciplinary Commission and Department of Professional Regulation. Mr. Tahmassebi has a handled and tried cases throughout the nation in both federal and state courts in Illinois, Indiana, Florida, New York, Wisconsin and California. Mr. Tahmassebi also represents a number of well-known professional athletes, including NFL and PGA professionals, in various matters such as litigation and contract negotiations.

Mr. Tahmassebi is currently a co-chair of the Chicago Bar Associations Committee for Professional Responsibility as well as a member of the Chicago Bar Association’s Judicial Evaluation Committee. He regularly speaks on legal ethics and how to avoid legal malpractice. Mr. Tahmassebi has been honored in the 2012-2019 Super Lawyers Publication in the area of legal malpractice.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Amir R. Tahmassebi is currently a partner at Konicek & Dillon and concentrates his practice in the areas of professional negligence, legal ethics, commercial litigation, casualty and sports law. He has successfully defended and prosecuted numerous lawyers, accountants, architects and engineers throughout the nation and has tried dozens of cases to verdict. Mr. Tahmassebi has successfully handled legal malpractice cases on a wide range of issues and recently obtained a defense verdict in a legal malpractice case seeking over ten million in damages. He has represented attorneys, accountants and other professionals in civil and administrative hearings before the Attorney Disciplinary Commission and Department of Professional Regulation. Mr. Tahmassebi has a handled and tried cases throughout the nation in both federal and state courts in Illinois, Indiana, Florida, New York, Wisconsin and California. Mr. Tahmassebi also represents a number of well-known professional athletes, including NFL and PGA professionals, in various matters such as litigation and contract negotiations.

Mr. Tahmassebi is currently a co-chair of the Chicago Bar Associations Committee for Professional Responsibility as well as a member of the Chicago Bar Association’s Judicial Evaluation Committee. He regularly speaks on legal ethics and how to avoid legal malpractice. Mr. Tahmassebi has been honored in the 2012-2019 Super Lawyers Publication in the area of legal malpractice.

attorneys.name: Christine K. Tani
attorneys.practice_type: Franchise Law Lawyers in Wheaton, IL
attorneys.bio:
Christine K. Tani heads the firm's Franchise Law Practice Group, along with Doris Carter.

Christine is a transactional attorney bringing over 40 years of experience representing franchisors, franchisees, and business clients. As part of her effort to assist her franchisor clients comply with state and federal franchise law, she conducts training sessions on franchise law compliance. Christine encourages and values ongoing communications between clients and attorneys, so that her clients have legal guidance regarding each aspect of their next project or transaction.

Christine comes to us most recently from the Wheaton Law firm of Carter & Tani. She was a founding partner, having established the firm with partner, Doris Adkins Carter, in 1991.

Prior to founding Carter & Tani, Christine was an in-house attorney for a national franchisor for 13 years. She represented the national franchisor in connection with franchise registrations nationwide.

Christine graduated from Beloit College Cum Laude with a Bachelor of Arts degree in Psychology. She attended Boston University Law School for two years, and transferred to Chicago Kent (IIT) School of Law, where she graduated with High Honors.

Christine is a member of the American Bar Association, the ABA Forum on Franchising, and the DuPage County Bar Association. She regularly attended the ABA Forum on Franchising annual law conferences in order to keep current with developments in franchise law.

In addition to her professional endeavors, Christine has been a volunteer with many organizations. She currently serves on the Finance Team of her church, where she has been a member for many years. She and her husband teach confirmation to 7th and 8th graders at her church. For the past 20 years, she has gone on mission trips both domestic and overseas, including Honduras, Costa Rica, Guatemala, Dominican Republic, New Orleans, Columbia, SC, Florida, and Biloxi, MS. On these mission trips she has built and/or repaired houses and done roofing. She has also volunteered with the local Habitat for Humanity affiliate in northern Illinois, including doing pro bono legal work.

For 13 years she served on the Board of Lifelink Corporation, a human services agency, formerly located in Bensenville, Illinois. She served as Chairman of the Lifelink Board for 2 years. For 12 years, she served on the Board of Advocate Health Care in Oak Brook, Illinois, the largest health system in the State of Illinois.

To achieve a work-life balance, Christine enjoys spending time with her husband, children and grandchildren, traveling, and biking. When the weather allows, she rides her bike to and from work (about 6 miles each way).

attorneys.name: David N. Tanner
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Law Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
David Tanner focuses his practice primarily in the areas of commercial real estate and corporate law, with a particular focus on: real estate acquisition, disposition, and development, including retail, office and industrial leasing, and property management; business planning, corporate formation and corporate acquisitions and dispositions for a variety of clients, including private equity clients and closely held businesses; representing both lenders and borrowers in commercial financing transactions, including loan workouts and restructurings; and the representation of developers, contractors, and subcontractors, in mechanics' lien and bond claim matters.

Prior to joining Carlson Partners, Ltd., David was a partner with Daspin & Aument, LLP in Chicago, Illinois where he focused primarily on commercial real estate transactions involving acquisitions, dispositions, leasing and financing of a variety of real estate asset classes, including retail, office, industrial, multi-family, and mixed use projects. In addition, David represented borrowers engaged in obtaining and refinancing construction, permanent, syndicated and other credit facilities totaling more than $300 million in loans. Prior to Daspin & Aument, LLP, David was an Associate with Gardner, Carton & Douglas, LLP (now known as Drinker, Biddle & Reath LLP) in Chicago, Illinois where he focused primarily on representing the commercial real estate needs of the largest retailer in the United States as well as those of the largest home builder in the United States. David also represented an Illinois pension fund in a variety of commercial real estate transactions. David also spent considerable time negotiating and drafting loan documents on behalf of lenders who made secured loans to borrowers in the real estate industry.

David is a member of the International Council of Shopping Centers, the American Bar Association and the Illinois State Bar Association. In 2008, David was named Illinois Super Lawyers Rising Star.

attorneys.name: Mary E. Taradash
attorneys.practice_type: Social Security Disability Lawyers in McHenry, IL
attorneys.bio:
Mary Taradash grew up in the ethnic neighborhoods of Chicago, immersed in cultural diversity and speaking Spanish and Lithuanian as well as English. After completing college, Mary worked for the State of Illinois Office of Education as Ombudsman, investigating and mediating education-related issues throughout the state. She completed graduate studies in communications and organizational psychology that propelled her into research, planning and evaluation for the Illinois Law Enforcement and the Dangerous Drugs Commissions in Chicago. However, it was her drive to make a difference to her world, one person at a time that compelled Mary to enter law school.

After more than 25 years of focus on family law throughout the metropolitan Chicago area, Mary now concentrates in social security disability where she has a direct and positive impact on people's lives. She views her current efforts as a natural extension of family practice, where the issues often included the impact of injuries, disability and financial distress.

Mary and her husband and law partner, Randy call McHenry County home and established their practice 38 years ago to serve this community and northern Illinois. They have two grown children and are both still committed to quality in the practice of law, social justice and making a difference to the community, its people and the environment.

attorneys.name: Daniel W. Tarpey
attorneys.practice_type: Business & Commercial Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
With over 16 years of business litigation experience, Dan Tarpey co-founded Tarpey Wix LLC with two goals in mind: (i) getting the result the client wants and nothing less; and (ii) achieving that result without breaking the bank in doing so. It is Dan's philosophy that a client should never feel like giving up before reaching the finish line because of discouraging legal fees. Coupling the talent that comes with being trained by, working under and ultimately becoming partners with, some of the most brilliant and skilled litigators in the country, with the personal attention and flexibility on fee arrangements in order to accomplish a client's goal is THE focus of our practice.

As a third generation Chicago trial lawyer, Dan grew up watching his grandfather, father and two older brothers try cases in Chicago court rooms. While such an upbringing may have led to quite a few "spirited" discussions around the Tarpey family dinner table, it made Dan the lawyer he is today. With a fierce competitive spirit coupled with a never-forgotten lesson drilled by his father that being a trial lawyer means you don't give up until there is justice, is what drives Dan's practice today. His close relationships with clients, many of which have become his close friends, are a testament to his brutally loyal commitment. Dan prides himself not only on being his clients' lawyer, but views being a trusted friend and advisor equally as important. Running his own practice now allows him to dedicate the time and energy to accomplishing those goals.

After graduating from the University of Notre Dame Law School, Dan embarked on a commercial litigation career, working for some of the biggest and most reputable firms in the country, ascending through the ranks and making partner at the earliest possible time he became eligible. Dan ultimately left partnership at his former firm in order to take control of his practice, give his clients the personal attention he feels they deserve and not feel the pressures of having to bill the client for every task or discussion.

Dan's practice involves all types of business-related litigation, with particular emphasis on contract , partnership/LLC and commercial real estate-related disputes. A significant part of Dan's practice also includes unfair competition, non-compete, executive compensation disputes, corporate espionage and other employment-related matters. While a litigator by background, Dan devotes substantial time counseling his clients how best to stay out of litigation. With 16 years of litigating contract-related matters under his belt, Dan has the litigator's perspective of seeing what can ultimately go wrong in a contractual relationship and use that experience to his clients' benefit on the front end. Dan's clients feel that a litigator's insight at the inception of contract brings significant value by diffusing colossal headaches before they happen.

attorneys.name: R. Kyle Tate
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Alton, IL
attorneys.bio:
R. Kyle Tate is an attorney at Simmons Hanly Conroy in the Complex Litigation Department. He joined the firm in 2019 and has more than 20 years of experience representing clients in complex legal cases. He focuses his practice on mass tort litigation cases that involve healthcare and privacy issues.

Attending to Details

Kyle is a vital member of the complex litigation team. His main responsibilities center around the evidentiary process, with a focus on multijurisdictional and domestic arbitration and federal and state court proceedings.

Kyle reviews defendant custodial files to prepare plaintiffs for depositions and identifies which information and documents will be most beneficial for use in pleadings, motions, depositions, and in the courtroom. He also conducts legal research and analyzes complex claims in multidistrict litigation, consulting with the litigation team regarding any new and existing policies that may affect their ability to adjudicate the matter and see it through to the closure of the case.

"A complex case can turn on one piece of evidence, one claim that is either answered or refuted," Kyle said. "In many cases we need to reach a critical mass to persuade the judiciary to certify a class, recognize a claim, or reach a settlement."

He deals with highly sensitive, privileged, and often private information of individuals; that carries a lot of responsibility.

"Technology allows us to focus the lens, but it still needs to be framed with solid legal analysis," he concluded.

A Client Culture

For Kyle, clients are so much more than a job to be completed; they're at the center of his consideration. When working a case, he steps into the client's situation and addresses challenges and obstacles that lie ahead in addition to their present struggles.

"It's about being efficient with time and addressing the client's needs in a thoughtful, engaging, and purposeful manner," he said. "Chairman John Simmons has created a culture where the enthusiasm for cases and clients is contagious, and that is representative in our culture, our firm, down to our families."

He explains that it starts from the moment clients hire the firm, with a well thought out onboarding experience. Simmons Hanly Conroy has invested in the right tools and is continually seeking to improve, creating the best possible journey for clients and their families.

"The clients we represent - from one individual to the whole class - deserve a team that will work with them around the clock and be responsive to fast-paced procedural matters, the evidentiary process, and conclusions that have solid legal foundations," Kyle said.

Background and Education

Prior to joining Simmons Hanly Conroy, Kyle headed his own firm for eight years, where he provided legal services to corporations, health care providers and nonprofit agencies regarding regulations and compliance with the PPACA and the ACA.

He also worked as assistant counsel for the St. Louis County Circuit Court and as policy advisor for Rep. Charles Portwood in Jefferson City, where he helped pass Missouri's "Ticket to Work" bill, helping many with disabilities return to work.

Kyle received a B.A. in History from University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign in 1995. He received his J.D. with a Certificate in Health Law from Saint Louis University School of Law in 2002. At SLU, he was named Student of the Year in 2002, served as lead editor for the Journal of Health Law from 2001-2002 and as an editor from 2000-2001.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
R. Kyle Tate is an attorney at Simmons Hanly Conroy in the Complex Litigation Department. He joined the firm in 2019 and has more than 20 years of experience representing clients in complex legal cases. He focuses his practice on mass tort litigation cases that involve healthcare and privacy issues.

Attending to Details

Kyle is a vital member of the complex litigation team. His main responsibilities center around the evidentiary process, with a focus on multijurisdictional and domestic arbitration and federal and state court proceedings.

Kyle reviews defendant custodial files to prepare plaintiffs for depositions and identifies which information and documents will be most beneficial for use in pleadings, motions, depositions, and in the courtroom. He also conducts legal research and analyzes complex claims in multidistrict litigation, consulting with the litigation team regarding any new and existing policies that may affect their ability to adjudicate the matter and see it through to the closure of the case.

"A complex case can turn on one piece of evidence, one claim that is either answered or refuted," Kyle said. "In many cases we need to reach a critical mass to persuade the judiciary to certify a class, recognize a claim, or reach a settlement."

He deals with highly sensitive, privileged, and often private information of individuals; that carries a lot of responsibility.

"Technology allows us to focus the lens, but it still needs to be framed with solid legal analysis," he concluded.

A Client Culture

For Kyle, clients are so much more than a job to be completed; they're at the center of his consideration. When working a case, he steps into the client's situation and addresses challenges and obstacles that lie ahead in addition to their present struggles.

"It's about being efficient with time and addressing the client's needs in a thoughtful, engaging, and purposeful manner," he said. "Chairman John Simmons has created a culture where the enthusiasm for cases and clients is contagious, and that is representative in our culture, our firm, down to our families."

He explains that it starts from the moment clients hire the firm, with a well thought out onboarding experience. Simmons Hanly Conroy has invested in the right tools and is continually seeking to improve, creating the best possible journey for clients and their families.

"The clients we represent - from one individual to the whole class - deserve a team that will work with them around the clock and be responsive to fast-paced procedural matters, the evidentiary process, and conclusions that have solid legal foundations," Kyle said.

Background and Education

Prior to joining Simmons Hanly Conroy, Kyle headed his own firm for eight years, where he provided legal services to corporations, health care providers and nonprofit agencies regarding regulations and compliance with the PPACA and the ACA.

He also worked as assistant counsel for the St. Louis County Circuit Court and as policy advisor for Rep. Charles Portwood in Jefferson City, where he helped pass Missouri's "Ticket to Work" bill, helping many with disabilities return to work.

Kyle received a B.A. in History from University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign in 1995. He received his J.D. with a Certificate in Health Law from Saint Louis University School of Law in 2002. At SLU, he was named Student of the Year in 2002, served as lead editor for the Journal of Health Law from 2001-2002 and as an editor from 2000-2001.

When he's not practicing law, Kyle enjoys spending time with his parents, sisters, nephew and niece.

After graduating from DePaul University's School of Law, Howard joined Soffietti, Johnson, Teegen, Argueta, Bawcum & Barone in 1971. Howard is also the acting Village Attorney for the Village of Fox Lake, a client that the firm has represented for over 28 years since 1981.

Howard brings over 41 years of experience in representing parties in construction, corporate and commercial related disputes, including breach of contract lawsuits, mechanic's lien cases and representation of banking institutions seeking to recover on mortgages and other collateral, along with handling business acquisitions and sales.

Howard's practice also includes the representation of commercial and residential land development companies in each phase of the land development process, ranging from land acquisition, the entitlement process, negotiations and agreements with local municipal and state entities, and ultimately, in some instances, the sale of developed property to interested parties, national builders and corporations.

Howard has developed throughout the years a reputation for being both a fearless advocate on behalf of his clients and a fair and reasonable adversary to his opponents.

Howard currently resides in Hawthorn Woods, Illinois, with his wife Barbara, with whom he has two children and six grandchildren.

attorneys.name: James Jeffrey Teich
attorneys.firm_name: Women’s Divorce & Family Law Group by Haid and Teich LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Family law Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Teich joined the Women's Divorce & Family Law Group in 2013 as a managing partner. Mr. Teich is a skilled and dedicated attorney who has extensive experience representing both men and women in family law cases in Illinois. He vehemently works to protect his client's rights in family law disputes. Mr. Teich's interest in women's rights dates as far back as law school, where, as a member of Law Review, he wrote an article concerning the issues of Battered Women's Syndrome. Mr. Teich became acutely aware of the lack of protection afforded women in family law cases when he began assisting female family members and friends in their cases. These experiences, in part, fueled his desire to join a group focused on protecting and advancing the rights of women and mothers.

Mr. Teich has vast knowledge and experience with respect to litigating divorce cases and post-decree cases (such as child support, custody, visitation, educational expenses, maintenance (formerly known as alimony), etc.), and will fiercely advocate on a client's behalf. At the same time, he is known for being a caring and even-handed attorney who puts the needs of his clients and their children first. Mr. Teich also works in the areas of adoption and the guardianship of minors.

Mr. Teich has been mentored by prominent women in the legal profession, including the Honorable Ann C. Williams of the Seventh Circuit United States Court of Appeals. He is also a member of the E-Women Network.

Mr. Teich has made multiple television appearances and appeared in periodicals (such as the Chicago Tribune) and online articles in connection with his divorce and custody cases. He is a co-author of the book Strategies For Family Law In Illinois. Additionally, he often speaks at conferences on family law issues.

Mr. Teich graduated with honors from Emory University in 1993 and graduated from Chicago-Kent College of Law with honors in 2000. Mr. Teich was the Executive Editor of the Chicago-Kent Law Review and was a recipient of a Scholarship for Academic Excellence. He also received two CALI Academic Achievement Awards.

Mr. Teich is admitted to practice law in the State of Illinois and the Northern District of Illinois. He is a member of the Chicago Bar Association and Illinois State Bar Association. Prior to practicing family law, Mr. Teich was an attorney in the corporate law department of McDermott, Will & Emery. While practicing corporate law Mr. Teich gained invaluable knowledge regarding the infrastructure, valuation and management of businesses. Mr. Teich often utilizes his business knowledge in family law matters where a party solely owns or has a partnership interest in a business.

attorneys.name: Stephen J. Telken
attorneys.practice_type: Asbestosis/Mesothelioma Lawyers in Edwardsville, IL
attorneys.bio:
Stephen J. Telken specializes in handling serious bodily injury and wrongful death claims arising from dangerous products, dangerous premises, trucking/vehicle accidents, and other acts of corporate and individual negligence.

Telken has devoted a significant amount of his practice to handling claims for injured railroad and river workers, under the Federal Employer's Liability Act (FELA) and Jones Act. He represents injured railroad workers and seamen, from several states, against numerous employers. Telken has successfully litigated claims against the major railroads and barge/towing companies, resulting in substantial jury verdicts and sizeable settlements.

In 1995, Telken earned his law degree (J.D.) and a Masters degree in Business Administration (M.B.A.) from St. Louis University . In 1991, he graduated from Rockhurst College , with a degree in Finance and Economics.

Telken spent his early years of practice working for a defense firm in St. Louis before shifting his practice to represent injured persons, in early 2001.

Telken is licensed in Missouri and Illinois as well as the federal courts in the Eastern District of Missouri and Southern District of Illinois. He appears in the state courts of Illinois , Missouri , and Indiana . Telken belongs to several professional organizations including the Missouri Bar, the Illinois Bar Association, the American Association for Justice, the Illinois Trial Lawyers Association and the Missouri Trial Lawyers Association.

I also write and publish articles in those areas of the law in which I concentrate, including divorce and personal injury.

attorneys.practice_type: Wrongful Death Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
Craig Tobin has been voted, by his peers to "The Best Lawyers in America," "Leading Lawyers", "Leading American Lawyers and Super Lawyers" His impressive trial successes in precedent-setting civil and criminal cases is why he is recognized nationally as one of the best trial lawyers in America.

Craig D. Tobin has once again been selected to the Best Lawyers in America. The law firm of Tobin & Muñoz, LLC has also been selected once again for inclusion in the Best Law Firms in America. Craig and the law firm have received this honor for more than 25 years. The selection process to Best Lawyers in America involves the votes of over 1 million attorneys throughout the United States.

Craig D. Tobin has been selected as an Illinois Super Lawyer again.

Craig D. Tobin has been recommended by his peers has a Leading Lawyer in civil rights/constitutional law, commercial litigation, criminal defense and personal injury.

Tobin has guided numerous clients through cases which attract intensive media coverage and have changed or defined the law.

Tobin began his career in the Cook County Public Defender's Office on the Murder Task Force. He tried numerous capital cases, and achieved an unprecedented number of acquittals in high profile cases. Mr. Tobin is an instructor and faculty member for the National Institute of Trial Advocacy (NITA). NITA is a premier provider of trial skills, training seminars and litigation-related publications for attorneys. He has given numerous lectures on the art of cross-examination and closing arguments.

Tobin founded Craig D. Tobin & Associates in 1985 when he left the Homicide Task Force of the Cook County Public Defender's Office. He was joined by the late Honorable Robert J. Collins (1911 - 1997). For over 25 years, Judge Collins sat as a felony court judge and also heard complex civil litigation. Prior to becoming a judge, Judge Collins was a well respected attorney who was the 1st Assistant United States Attorney for the Northern District of Illinois and an Assistant Corporation Counsel for the City of Chicago. Judge Collins argued landmark cases on behalf of the city before the Illinois and US Supreme Court. Judge Collins was called by bar associations and the Chicago Tribune "the standard by which all other judges are to be measured."

Craig Tobin is regularly featured in publications including the Chicago Tribune and American Bar Journal. He graduated from Chicago Kent College of Law in 1980 with high honors and the University of Illinois/Chicago in 1976 with honors. He is a member of Illinois State Bar Association and the Illinois Trial Lawyers Association (ATLA).

attorneys.name: Darryl Tom
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
Darryl Tom is experienced in all areas of public finance and tax-exempt bond practice, and has served as co-bond counsel, issuer's counsel, and underwriters counsel on municipal finance transactions having represented the State of Illinois, the City of Chicago, the Chicago Board of Education, the Chicago Park District, and the Chicago Transit Authority.

Mr. Tom is also experienced in commercial litigation; specifically, in the areas of product liability, consumer fraud, insurance fraud, corporate transactional disputes, marine/surface transportation litigation, construction litigation, and subrogation. He has managed a variety of cases from inception through discovery, to trial and appeal.

Mr. Tom received his Juris Doctor from Northwestern University School of Law, Chicago, in 1995 and a Bachelor of Arts in economics from Cornell University in 1992.

Mr. Tom is licensed to practice law in Illinois and is also admitted to the Trial Bar of the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois.

Mr. Tom was named a 2009 Business Leader of Color by Chicago United and was also a Leadership Greater Chicago fellow from 1999-2000. He is past president of the Chinese American Bar Association, and has been heavily involved in the local Asian community. He is a past director of the Asian American Alliance, president and director of the Chinatown Chamber of Commerce, vice president and director of the Chinese American Service League, and past executive vice-president of the Organization of Chinese Americans Chicago Chapter. Mr. Tom is also a past board member of the Erie Family Health Center.

attorneys.name: Thomas W. Toolis
attorneys.practice_type: Corporate Law Lawyers in Frankfort, IL
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Thomas W. Toolis was born and raised in Chicago and is a graduate of Brother Rice High School and the University of Illinois at Chicago, where he majored in accounting. After passing the C.P.A. exam, Thomas worked as an accountant at Rush University prior to earning a Juris Doctor from Kent College of Law in Chicago. Since starting his legal career, Thomas has focused his practice on bankruptcy, corporate law, and real estate law while at Jahnke, Sullivan and Toolis.

Thomas believes in providing excellent service for each client, no matter what the circumstances and time involved. As a father of three, he understands the stress many families face when confronted with difficult situations. Thomas strives to work closely with his clients to resolve those issues, so that the clients can feel confident and trusting in the process. He also recognizes that the law can be intimidating to those without his specialized training. Therefore, it is important to Thomas that he provides his clients with an informal, personal level, in order to ensure that his clients understand each step.

To date, Thomas has discharged over $50 million in debt for his clients, providing them with a chance for a new beginning. He has also aided over 500 corporations with incorporation and transactional disputes. Thomas also believes strongly in planning for families for the long term. He is also skilled at drafting wills and trusts to help families provide for their loved ones. Thomas specializes in special needs trusts, life insurance trusts, and estate planning for business owners.

He has served as the President of the Orland Park Area Chamber of Commerce, which boasts over 650 members due in part to Thomas's leadership.

attorneys.name: Joseph C. Torres
attorneys.practice_type: Labor Law Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
Joseph (Joe) Torres is a Partner at Karmel & Torres, LLC., and is experienced in all areas of labor and employment law. Focusing on representing public and private companies, Joe has extensive experience in administrative, grievance, and arbitration proceedings, as well as state and federal court. In addition to traditional labor law representation, Joe’s expertise includes the Illinois Workers’ Compensation Act, state and federal discrimination, and anti-retaliation law.

Joe serves as outside counsel for unions representing retail and commercial food workers, cannabis workers, nurses, and auto and defense manufacturer workers across various legal areas. These areas include labor issues before the National Labor Relations Board (NLRB), contract and disciplinary interpretation issues, administrative investigations and hearings, and other types of employment litigation. Joe is also an expert at developing and carrying out legal strategies in support of union organizing and contract campaigns.

As one of the nation's leading union-side cannabis attorneys, Joe advises cannabis unions from the ground-up. This includes being heavily involved in initial organizing campaigns. Joe negotiated Illinois’ first cannabis collective bargaining agreements, earning significant wage and benefit increases for workers. Relatedly, Joe has successfully litigated against cannabis employers in NLRB proceedings, protecting cannabis workers’ right to organize under the National Labor Relations Act.

Joe serves as outside counsel for unions representing retail and commercial food workers, cannabis workers, nurses, and auto and defense manufacturer workers across various legal areas. These areas include labor issues before the National Labor Relations Board (NLRB), contract and disciplinary interpretation issues, administrative investigations and hearings, and other types of employment litigation. Joe is also an expert at developing and carrying out legal strategies in support of union organizing and contract campaigns.

As one of the nation's leading union-side cannabis attorneys, Joe advises cannabis unions from the ground-up. This includes being heavily involved in initial organizing campaigns. Joe negotiated Illinois’ first cannabis collective bargaining agreements, earning significant wage and benefit increases for workers. Relatedly, Joe has successfully litigated against cannabis employers in NLRB proceedings, protecting cannabis workers’ right to organize under the National Labor Relations Act.

attorneys.bio:
Andrea Torgrimson has worked tirelessly for her clients since 2017 at the Illinois Hammer. Andrea started in 2017 as an associate attorney and, through her diligence and dedication to clients, has been promoted to Junior Partner. She has helped hundreds of clients financially recover from the personal injuries they’ve sustained, and is excited to bring that passion and commitment to our firm.

Andrea comes to us all the way from New Mexico! She received her law degree from DePaul University College of Law. While in undergrad, Andrea worked in a hospital. After witnessing first-hand the injuries sustained by people, through no fault of their own, and how much help they needed, she realized her passion was to work as an attorney in the realm of personal injury.

Andrea currently specializes in litigation, especially for premises liability cases. Early in Andrea’s career, she was drawn to more complex cases, particularly those where establishing liability took substantial effort and thorough investigation of evidence. Andrea knew from the first trial she attended that she wanted to specialize in litigation and fighting for people in court.

When she’s not working for the betterment of her clients, she enjoys attending food festivals, spending time with her furry friends, and binging TV shows with her husband. Andrea also plays indoor beach volleyball throughout the year, enjoys running, biking, and cooking.

Andrea feels extremely passionate about her clients’ causes and is driven to help others who are in need. She doesn’t take no for an answer and is unafraid of confrontation.

attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Transactional and Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
Jasmina is a commercial transactional and commercial litigation attorney with extensive experience which started with litigating sophisticated commercial disputes, and then expanded to all areas of transactional business law and commercial real estate. After helping several clients sell their businesses and being asked: what should I do now? Jasmina added estate planning and estate and trust administration to the services that she offers to her clients. Jasmina finds great satisfaction in helping commercial and individual clients reach their business and personal goals in buying, selling, growing, downsizing and planning for their future along the way.

Jasmina’s legal skills developed over more than twenty-five years of training by first-class litigators and mentors, as well as practical, hands-on experience in transactions. Small and mid-sized business, as well as many business owners, have found Jasmina to be a trusted source for legal advice and counsel. Substantively, her legal experience includes: business torts, contracts, creditors rights, corporate governance, fiduciary obligations, unfair competition, consumer class actions, restrictive covenant enforcement and defense and other areas of law applicable to businesses and professionals.

Jasmina graduated, magna cum laude, from the University of Illinois College of Law in 1998. She earned her Bachelor of Arts degree from the University of Illinois at Chicago and is admitted to practice in Illinois and before the U. S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois.Jasmina has a passion for language and speaks Serbian and Spanish, and is conversant in French, German and Greek.

attorneys.name: Helena L. Trachtenberg
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Rolling Meadows, IL
attorneys.bio:
As a Partner at the Cooper Trachtenberg Law Group, LLC, Helena L. Trachtenberg focuses her practice exclusively on family law matters. Working out of the firm's offices in Rolling Meadows, Illinois, she provides astute representation to clients throughout Cook, Lake, and DuPage counties as well as other parts of the greater Chicago metropolitan area. Ms. Trachtenberg, who is fluent in both English and Russian and admitted to practice before all Illinois and Florida state courts, has received an "Excellent" peer review rating through Avvo for both her successful track record and for the ethical way she handles what are often complex, emotional cases. She has also been named to The National Advocates: Top 40 Under 40 and to The 10 Best Attorneys Under 40 for Client Satisfaction. Additionally, she serves on the Advisory Board of DePaul University’s Family Law Center. In 2024 Ms. Trachtenberg became a Fellow of the American Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers following a rigorous, competitive application process.

Ms. Trachtenberg's practice is largely centered on representing people whose marriages are coming to an end and who face such divorce-related issues as alimony and child support, the division of complex marital assets and debts, and parental responsibilities and parenting time. A forceful courtroom advocate for her clients, when necessary, she also helps many of them attempt to reach accord on some of these matters through the negotiation of settlement agreements. Ms. Trachtenberg is a trained mediator, collaborative law professional and is on the list of approved attorneys who can serve as a guardian ad litem. She is additionally a Parenting Coordinator helping high conflict families avoid returning to the court system.

Ms. Trachtenberg, a native of Minsk, Belarus, is a graduate of the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign where she earned a bachelor's degree in international trade policy and development in 2007. She is a 2010 graduate of the University of Miami School of Law, and she served an internship with the 11th Judicial Circuit Court of Florida. Beyond the practice of law, Ms. Trachtenberg is an active member of several voluntary professional associations including: Northwest Suburban Bar Association, Collaborative Divorce Illinois, Lake County Bar Association, Chicago Bar Association and Florida Bar Association.

attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
Selected as a 2014 Rising Star by Super Lawyers Magazine

Julie H. Trepeck

online at

visit superlawyers.com

Recognized for excellence in leadership & legal practice in the 2010-2011 Edition of Cambridge Who's Who

Julie Trepeck is an Owner and Partner of Trepeck Bane, P.C., d/b/a Chicago Debt Solutions.

Ms. Trepeck started her own firm to make a greater impact on the lives of people struggling with debt. Julie understands the bankruptcy process and what clients need while going through it. She always displays a great deal of compassion and professionalism. She believes the bankruptcy laws provide a great justice to those seeking financial relief. Her years of experience allow her to represent her clients aggressively, yet with great knowledge on the subject and of the Code. Julie has encountered a variety of issues while practicing bankruptcy, always facing the issues head on with each case she conducts.

Ms. Trepeck has assisted thousands of people in all stages of debt solution and works effectively to advocate for each and every one of her clients. She has consulted individuals and business owners to get a fresh start or reorganize their financial lives.

Prior to starting this firm, Julie had experience working at other firms in the bankruptcy world. She worked extensively with bankruptcy, debt settlement, divorce, real estate and general motion practice. With a focus on bankruptcy, both Chapter 7 and Chapter 13 cases, she started out her bankruptcy career with the largest bankruptcy firm in the United States. While there, she became one of the managing attorneys for the Chicago office and with that managing team, she helped lead the firm's education and training of all new attorneys. Additionally, she provided an integral part to refine the internal processes of the firm. She refined the process to make it more efficient, not only internally, but also for clients. Just after law school, Julie had her own company, Foreclosure Associates, LLC where she assisted homeowners in forbearances, loan modifications or other options in an effort to help people save their homes. Her knowledge of the foreclosure process is extensive and allowed her to represent clients and get them the relief they needed.

Julie Trepeck attended undergrad at the University of Michigan and graduated with Honors. She then went on to law school in Chicago, at Chicago-Kent College of Law which brought her to Chicago. Julie is currently licensed in both Illinois and Michigan with her practice of bankruptcy taking place in Illinois. She is also licensed to practice in the federal district court for the Northern District of Illinois.

attorneys.bio:
Aaron T. Troy is a Director in the Trusts and Estates Practice Area, focusing his practice primarily on advising individuals and families on estate planning objectives and asset protection strategies.

Aaron believes estate planning is far more "art" than "science," and evaluates his clients' goals from a wide range of perspectives. He annually prepares federal gift and generation-skipping transfer tax returns, as well as federal and Illinois estate tax returns. Aaron also represents executors and trustees in complex estate and trust administration matters, including estate and trust litigation.

Aaron also assists clients in applying for guardianship for minors and adults with disabilities. In DuPage County, Aaron has been court-appointed to serve as counsel for minors and adults with disabilities in guardianship cases.

Aaron is a volunteer member of the Board of Directors of Tabor Hills Health Care Facility, a senior living campus in Naperville that U.S. News and World Report consistently ranks as one of the top senior living facilities in the United States.

Prior to joining Huck Bouma, Aaron was an associate at the Wheaton law firm of Rolewick & Gutzke P.C.

attorneys.name: Joseph Tully
attorneys.practice_type: Business Services Lawyers in Wheaton, IL
attorneys.bio:
Joseph W. Tully was an esteemed attorney with over 40 years of experience, licensed to practice law in Illinois and Arizona. In 2015, his law practice merged with that of Huck Bouma.

His practice was concentrated in the areas of estate planning, trust administration, probate, and business services. By employing proven and effective techniques, Joe enabled his estate planning clients to minimize taxation and avoid the costs and delays associated with probate.

Joe served as counsel to many small business entities, advising business owners on tax and other matters, and providing advice on business succession planning.

Joe and his wife, Karen Sakash PhD, resided in Chicago and also spent time at their residence in Cochise County, Arizona. They are the proud parents of three adult daughters: Elisabeth, Katherine, and Sarah.

Joe enjoyed fishing, golf, poker, and riding his all-terrain vehicle. His legacy continues through his contributions to the legal field and the many lives he touched.

attorneys.name: Jane Elizabeth Unsell
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Wood River, IL
attorneys.bio:
Jane Unsell graduated from Oklahoma City University Law School at the top of her class in 1979. Following her admission to the Illinois and Oklahoma bars, Ms. Unsell began her private practice with the Madison County law firm of Bernard and Davidson located in Granite City, Illinois. She remained there until 1986, at which time she opened her own law practice in East Alton, Illinois. During her work at Bernard and Davidson, Ms. Unsell prepared and tried multiple cases before Madison and St. Clair County, Illinois juries. She has represented insurance companies, defended individuals and prosecuted claims for injured parties. In 1995, after leaving Bernard and Davidson and opening the law office of Unsell & Unsell she obtained a jury verdict for an injured plaintiff in an auto/truck which was recorded as the largest plaintiff verdict at the time in Macoupin County, Illinois. At present she focuses her practice primarily on representing clients injured in motor vehicle accidents. Additionally, she represents individuals who have been wrongfully denied insurance coverage. She also handles contested estate and guardianship cases, she now sits as a hearing panel member for the Attorney Registration and Disciplinary Commission in Springfield, Illinois. Mrs. Unsell is the senior partner in the law firm of Unsell, Schattnik & Phillips, PC which she founded in 1992. In 2010 she relocated the office from East Alton to Wood River, Illinois.

attorneys.name: Samantha S. Unsell
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Belleville, IL
attorneys.bio:
Samantha S. Unsell was born and raised in Southern Illinois by two lawyers. Her mother, a successful attorney, set an example of hard work, advocacy, and devotion to both career and family that helped shape Sam’s approach to the practice of law.

She earned her Bachelor of Philosophy in 2005 and her Juris Doctor in 2008 from Saint Louis University. While in law school, Sam worked as a law clerk at the firm, where she was mentored by Tom Keefe, one of the most respected trial lawyers in Illinois. Under his guidance, she learned how to prepare cases for trial and advocate effectively for injured clients. After passing the Illinois Bar, she joined the firm in 2009 and was named Partner on October 1, 2015.

Sam concentrates her practice on all personal injury matters, including medical malpractice, wrongful death, and automobile/trucking accidents. She is licensed to practice in both Illinois and Missouri.

Outside of the office, Sam enjoys spending time with her husband and three spirited daughters, reading, practicing yoga, and maintaining order in a household that also includes two English mastiffs.

attorneys.name: Laura M. Urbik Kern Esq.
attorneys.firm_name: Law Offices of Laura M. Urbik Kern
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Hinsdale, IL
attorneys.bio:
I recognize that you have a choice in attorneys and all family law attorneys CAN ultimately resolve your problem. The questions you must ask are: "Will the attorney I choose work to dismantle my marriage as carefully as it was originally built? Will my children be the #1 priority throughout the process? Will my lawyer explain the process and recognize that my life will be forever changed from this point forward?"

Our practice is a client-centered, team approach: your life, your decisions. Our Chicago divorce attorney will guide you, lay out your options, and try to teach you conflict resolution methods that you may use in the future. Your family unit needs to be dismantled with the same care with which it was built. Our goal is to try to preserve family principles while resolving your problems.

Call or contact our office for more information about how Chicago divorce attorney Laura M. Urbik Kern can help you resolve your family law disputes. She understands what you need from your legal counsel and can represent you in matters of divorce, allocation of parental responsibilities or parenting time, property division, juvenile law, and guardianship.

attorneys.name: Julian Manual Valdes
attorneys.firm_name: Nathan J. Noble, P.C., Attorney at Law
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Belvidere, IL
attorneys.bio:
My name is Julian M. Valdes, and I am an attorney primarily practicing in Boone and Winnebago Counties in Northern Illinois. I am a native to Belvidere, Illinois, and I hope to serve the community I was raised in however I can.

During law school, I worked for small law firms in Belvidere and Murphysboro, Illinois, primarily working cases in family law and civil litigation. During my time at Reed, Heller, Mansfield & Gross (now Reed, Heller & Cannell) in Murphysboro, Illinois, I worked under the City Attorney for the City of Murphysboro, Illinois by drafting ordinances, assisting in the prosecution of ordinance violations, and conducting research for a constitutional challenge to a local ordinance.

Following law school, I served as a law clerk to the Honorable Alberto C. Lamorena, III in the Superior Court of Guam. During my time as a law clerk for the Presiding Judge, I worked on a wide variety of matters ranging from criminal motions and trials (DUI, criminal sexual conduct, theft) to civil litigation and family law matters. I also had the opportunity to assist the Judiciary of Guam with litigation involving the Judiciary in the U.S. District Court of Guam.

Currently, I am an Associate Attorney for Nathan J. Noble, P.C. in Belvidere, Illinois. My practice revolves mostly around family law and civil litigation but also includes personal injury, estate planning, and real estate. I am eager to assist those who need help to the best of my abilities. Please do not hesitate to reach out to me and my office should you require legal services!
