attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
Nicole Valenti serves as the Senior Partner and Chief Compliance Officer at Taege Law Offices. Since 2014, Nicole has been an integral part of the firm, bringing her keen intellect and unwavering dedication to the practice of family law. Nicole's professional journey, from Associate Attorney to her current senior role, reflects her commitment to legal excellence and her deep passion for family law.

Nicole's clients regard her as honest, dedicated, and trustworthy. Her ability to communicate effectively and transparently ensures that her clients are informed and empowered throughout their legal journey. She is known for her thorough understanding of the law, strategic thinking, and problem-solving capabilities, all of which are instrumental in navigating the complexities of family law.

With a knack for attention to detail, Nicole has honed her ability to deliver meticulously crafted arguments that incorporate effective and persuasive legal writing. She has extensive litigation experience and has focused her entire practice in the area of family law, where her knowledgeable and strategic approach has consistently yielded favorable results for her clients.

Beyond her work at Taege Law Offices, Nicole's dedication to the community is evident in her voluntary work as a Guardian Ad Litem and Child Representative for Chicago Volunteer Legal Services. Here, she represents children in dissolution of marriage and parentage proceedings, ensuring their rights and interests are safeguarded.

Nicole's practical experience is enriched by her tenure with the Public Defender's Office under a 711 License. Further, her participation in the Restorative Justice Program underscores her commitment to a holistic and healing approach to legal disputes, enriching her understanding of family law and contributing to her skill as a dynamic attorney.

Nicole Valenti personifies the ethos of Taege Law Offices, delivering professional, refined, and dedicated service to her clients. She strives to maintain the highest levels of compliance and is relentless in her pursuit of providing expert, strategic legal advice in family law matters.

attorneys.name: Katie VanDeusen
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Hoffman Estates, IL
attorneys.bio:
(also known as Katie C. VanDeusen, Katie Colleen VanDeusen, Katie C. Galanes, Katie Colleen Galanes)

Katie knows divorce isn't easy. Where many shut themselves off to their client's emotional state, Katie chooses to fully engage instead.

"I understand that these are very difficult times, so I try to come up with a plan to help you move forward with the next step in your life in the most amicable way possible. I try to be a listener and take into account peoples' goals and concerns as it relates to their particular case." - Attorney Katie VanDeusen

Her empathy and compassionate style makes her a fierce and effective presence in the courtroom. Every day, Katie uses her unique perspective and strong work ethic to provide a fresh perspective for her clients.

No matter what brings you to her office, you can always expect patient guidance and thoughtful advice throughout the process. But in addition, Katie will take guidance from you: her client's goals and concerns shape how she approaches each case.

She's happy to provide helpful advice, both legally and confidentially. With Katie, you always know she's looking out for your best interests.

No family law issue is too challenging - attorney Katie VanDeusen is skilled in handling divorce, child support, paternity, resolution of parenting responsibilities, asset evaluations, and any other problem you might run into. Additionally, she is adept at handling post-decree issues such as college contributions or modifications to existing support.

Detail-oriented and passionate, no stone will be left unturned when Katie is on your side. Whether you're facing a divorce for the first time, or need help enforcing orders you'll be in good hands.

Managing Partner Katie VanDeusen was selected to the 2021 Illinois Rising Stars list. Katie has received this honor each year since 2018! This accolade is presented to outstanding, up-and-coming lawyers who are either under the age of 40 or who have been practicing for 10 years or less. Attorneys are selected by the Super Lawyers research team based on statewide surveys, peer and third-party nominations, and professional achievements. This is a huge honor - only 2.5% of Illinois attorneys receive this prestigious recognition each year.

In 2008, Katie graduated from the University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign before going to law school. She earned her Juris Doctor from The John Marshall Law School, graduating cum laude in 2011. While in law school, her interest in family law was sparked when she served as a judicial intern in the Domestic Relations Division of the Circuit Court of Cook County. Even before graduating, she became very familiar with the difficult issues people face and was determined to make it her area of practice.

An active member of the community, Katie knows the western suburbs well and grew up in Wheaton, Illinois.

Outside of work, Katie enjoys spending her free time relaxing and having fun with family and friends. She also loves running and staying active, completing her first half marathon in 2015.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Moline, IL
attorneys.bio:
Dennis VanDerGinst is the President/CEO of VanDerGinst Law, one of the most successful personal injury law firms in the country. He has been a tireless advocate for his clients and a stalwart ambassador for his profession. As a result, he has been recognized as one of the best in the country by clients, peers, and other professionals.

Dennis received his law degree from DePaul University in Chicago. He is licensed to practice in Illinois, Iowa, Washington D.C., and the federal courts. During his career he has represented clients in almost every state of the country. The focus of his practice has been on helping injured people. The law firm which bears his name has represented over 50,000 injury victims during his career, in all areas of personal injury law including but not limited to: motor vehicle accidents, product liability, premises liability, medical malpractice, nursing home abuse and neglect, worker’s compensation, mass and class actions, and all types of negligence cases.

His dedication to his clients has earned Dennis and his firm the prestigious Torch Award for Ethics, awarded by the Better Business Bureau, marking the first time this honor was ever bestowed upon a lawyer or law firm in the region. Dennis has also been awarded the Client’s Choice Award from AVVO Lawyer Rating Service and Client Champion recognition from Martindale-Hubbell, the most established attorney rating service in the profession. In In 2018, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2024 Dennis was voted as the Best Attorney in Eastern Iowa and Western Illinois in a survey conducted by the Quad-City Times. He was runner-up for that honor in 2019.

Dennis’s accomplishments and expertise within the profession have also won him accolades from his peers. He is rated AV Preeminent by Martindale-Hubbell Attorney Rating Service (the highest available rating) He has been designated a Super Lawyer by Thomson Reuters, a staple in the legal profession, and has been rated Superb with a 10/10 rating from AVVO Lawyer Rating Service. Chicago Lawyer magazine has recognized Dennis as one of the Top Injury Lawyers in Illinoisand the Iowa Association for Justice has featured him in an article in IAJ’s magazine, Iowa Trial Lawyer.

Dennis has been recognized as a “Top 100 Trial Lawyer”, by the National Trial Lawyers, an exclusive organization composed of the premier trial lawyers from across the country. Similarly, he has been selected for the following Specialty Recognitions of the NTL:

Top 25 Brain Injury Trial Lawyer

Top 10 Asbestos/Mesothelioma Trial Lawyer

Top 25 Medical Malpractice Trial Lawyer

Top 25 Motor Vehicle Accident Trial Lawyer

Top 10 Nursing Home Trial Lawyer

Top 25 Product Liability Trial Lawyer

Top 10 Trucking Trial Lawyer

He has likewise been selected as one of the top attorneys in the nation by the National Association of Distinguished Counsel, the American Trial Lawyers Association, Premier Lawyers of America, and the American Society of Legal Advocates, among others.

His success in the field of personal injury law is illustrated by his inclusion in the Multi-Million-Dollar Advocates Forum, whose membership is limited to those attorneys who have secured multi-million-dollar verdicts and settlements, which he has done dozens of times in his career.

His expertise has made him a reliable source of law-related information for numerous media outlets. He is often called upon to speak about legal and consumer issues in the news. He has been featured on the National Public Radio program, America’s Premier Lawyers, as well as on numerous regional and national radio and television programs and podcasts. In fact, he is the host of a very popular podcast, Legal Squeaks, which addresses legal and consumer issues which may impact ordinary people in their everyday lives.

He has been profiled in Fortune magazine, and numerous news and/or law-related publications. Similarly, he has authored numerous legal articles in professional journals and magazines and has been an active speaker/lecturer at regional and national conferences, conventions, seminars, and webinars that focus on the importance of personal injury law. In addition, Dennis has taught Torts and Insurance law as an adjunct professor.

He has been an extremely active member of several professional organizations such as the American Bar Association, the American Association for Justice, the Illinois and Iowa State Bar Associations, the Illinois Trial Lawyers Association, and the Iowa Association for Justice.

Dennis has served on the Board of Managers for the Illinois Trial Lawyers Association, the Board of Governors for the Iowa Association for Justice, and the Board of Trustees for the Pound Civil Justice Institute. He has also served as the State Delegate to AAJ for both Illinois and Iowa – the only person to ever serve in that capacity for both of those states. Additionally, he has served on the National Advisory Board for the National Crime Victims Bar Association and for the Association of Plaintiff Interstate Trucking Lawyers of America.

His career accomplishments have earned him the Albert Nelson Marquis Lifetime Achievement Award from Who’s Who, the Lifetime Achievement Award from Premier Lawyers of America, and the Best Attorney-Lifetime Charter Membership from Rue Ratings’ Best Attorneys of America.

Through his stewardship VanDerGinst Law became one of the first law firms in the country to embrace the powerful potential of the internet. The firm’s award-winning website, www.VLaw.com, has become a legal resource for other law firms, law students and lay people across the country. The VanDerGinst Law Facebook page is one of the most “liked” attorney Facebook pages in the world.

In addition to consumer and legal news, the firm often uses their online platforms to present cases and legal issues to focus groups and online mock juries.

Perhaps most important, Dennis has created a corporate culture at VanDerGinst Law which embraces the firm’s responsibilities as ambassadors of the profession and leaders in the community.

The Mission of VanDerGinst Law, as authored by Dennis, is:

To help people both in and out of the courtroom. In the courtroom the firm’s focus is on assisting those who have become injured or infirm on the job or due to the wrongdoing of others. Outside of the courtroom the firm’s focus is on helping those least able to help themselves, including the injured and infirm, the elderly and children. Additionally, the firm focuses on giving back to those to whom we all owe a debt of gratitude including first responders, veterans and active military, teachers, and front-line health care workers.

To that end, his law firm has donated millions of dollars and countless hours to the organizations that support these initiatives and advance growth and prosperity in their communities. In recognition of his character and philanthropic efforts, Dennis was recognized by GQ’s “Better Men, Better World” campaign.

In addition to his management responsibilities to the firm, Dennis oversees all injury cases and maintains an active caseload himself. He divides his time between each office and conducts Zoom meetings with all attorneys and staff each morning.

As the son of immigrants from both Cuba and Nicaragua, he knows the struggle of families who want nothing more than to become Americans and make the United States their true home. After completing his Bachelor of Arts degree in Philosophy with Summa Cum Laude honors at Florida International University, Matthew obtained his Juris Doctor from FIU’s College of Law in 2017. Matthew is an active member of the Florida State Bar and the American Bar Association, having had the privilege of representing both individuals and families in all manner of cases before the United States Citizenship and Immigration Service, Executive Office of Immigration Review, and the Board of Immigration Appeals.

attorneys.bio: Johnny Velázquez-Navarro is a licensed attorney and notary public with a Juris Doctor and a Bachelor's degree in Public Administration and Labor Relations, both earned with honors from the Pontifical Catholic University of Puerto Rico. He also holds a minor in Sociology. With a profound understanding of federal and state laws, public administration, and government affairs, Mr. Velázquez-Navarro is a highly motivated and accomplished professional known for his exceptional verbal communication, critical thinking, and analytical skills. While pursuing his degrees, Mr. Velázquez-Navarro was actively involved in various student organizations, assuming leadership roles within their governing bodies. He also participated in competitive debate tournaments, emerging victorious in the 27th edition of the National Debate Tournament Don Miguel Velázquez in Puerto Rico in 2022. Before joining CLG, Mr. VelázquezNavarro gained extensive experience with the federal government, participating in a foreclosure mediation program and contributing to a criminal law clinic. He also engaged in comprehensive legal research and analysis during a law clerkship, providing support on civil cases in Puerto Rico. As an attorney, Mr. Velázquez-Navarro demonstrates remarkable commitment, motivation, and professionalism, with a dedication to making a positive impact in his clients' cases. He is proficient in both English and Spanish. He is committed to helping others navigate the complex legal system in the United States, fostering a respectful and inclusive environment while driving results and continuous improvement.

attorneys.name: Thomas L. Veith
attorneys.practice_type: Family, Matrimonial, Domestic Relations Lawyers in Jacksonville, IL
attorneys.bio:
Thomas L. Veith joined Bellatti, Fay, Bellatti & Beard in 1990, and became a partner in 1993.

Tom graduated from Illinois College with a Bachelor of Arts degree in Accounting (summa cum laude 1986). While at Illinois College, he sat for the CPA exam, which he passed in May, 1986. He received his Juris Doctor from the University of North Carolina in 1989.

In 1988, Tom clerked with the law firm of Cain, Hibbard, Myers & Cook in Pittsfield, Massachusetts. He then joined that firm as an associate in 1989. While there, he concentrated primarily in litigation with a special emphasis on insurance defense.

Tom is a general practitioner. He has an extensive collection practice representing local and area businesses in Morgan, Scott, Cass, Pike, Brown and Schuyler Counties. He is also willing to serve as local counsel for other collection attorneys to alleviate time-consuming travel. Over the years, he has developed an extensive municipal practice. He prosecutes ordinance violations for the Cities of Jacksonville and Beardstown. He serves as the Attorney for the Village of Ashland and City of Virginia.

Tom practices estate planning, will and trust preparation, and trust and estate administration. This practice includes individual and estate and trust tax analysis and preparation.

Additionally, his practice includes matrimonial and family law. He has assisted husbands and wives through the difficult process of divorce, as well as representing parents in child custody, visitation, paternity, child support, and college educational expense matters. From time to time he has aided victims of domestic abuse with orders of protection. The scope of his practice includes real estate law, business law, and collegiate law.

Tom holds weekday appointments in Jacksonville. He also sees clients at West Central Bank in Ashland every Thursday morning. He has accepted referrals from the Midwest Center on Law and the Deaf.

Tom is a member of both the Morgan County Bar Association, for which he served as president in 2001, and the Illinois State Bar Association. He is a past member of the Massachusetts State and Berkshire County (Massachusetts) Bar Associations.

Tom has served the Jacksonville community on various boards and committees. These include the Crisis Center Foundation, the Wells Center, the Illinois Foundation for Deaf Children, and the Nursery School. He currently serves on the Board of Directors for Passavant Area Hospital, where he has held the offices of Treasurer, Vice Chair, and Chairman of the Board. He taught Business Law at Illinois College from 1995 - 2015. Occasionally he has given seminars on special needs trusts to parents of disabled children at the Illinois School for the Visually Impaired.

attorneys.name: Alissa Carter Verson
attorneys.practice_type: Franchise Law Lawyers in Wheaton, IL
attorneys.bio:
Alissa Carter Verson is a Director in the Franchise Law Practice Group. She focuses her practice on franchise law and related services, representing franchisors and subfranchisors in all 50 states and Illinois franchisees.

Alissa represents franchisors at all stages of growth, from start-up franchisors establishing franchise systems, to emerging franchisors, to established franchisors with small to large franchise systems. Alissa believes in providing efficient, thorough, and friendly service, and honest and direct communication.

Alissa is skilled at advising and counseling franchisor clients on the structuring of complex franchise systems, franchisee relationship matters, risk management, and compliance with federal and state franchise registration and disclosure laws and state relationship laws. The services Alissa provides to franchisors include drafting Franchise Disclosure Documents, Franchise Agreements, Multi-Unit Development Agreements, and other agreements related to franchise systems.

Alissa's franchise law interests also include reviewing Franchise Disclosure Documents and Franchise Agreements for prospective Franchisees, conducting Franchise Law Compliance Training for her franchisor clients, and assisting franchisors in engaging local counsel for international expansion.

Alissa also offers ancillary services to her franchise clients, including trademark registration and maintenance, commercial lease review, and the purchase and sale of franchised businesses.

Alissa comes to us most recently from the Wheaton franchise law firm of Carter & Tani where she had 7 years of experience in franchise law, representing franchisors, subfranchisors, and franchisees.

Outside of work, Alissa enjoys spending time with her husband, daughter, parents, and family pets. She enjoys camping, biking and hiking, reading, and traveling the world. Since 2021, she has served her community as a Plan Commissioner for the Village of Lombard Plan Commission.

attorneys.name: Nestor Vicario
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
Nestor Vicario has been an immigration attorney since 2014. His primary focus is family-based immigration, citizenship, hardship waivers of inadmissibility, Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA), and removal defense. Mr. Vicario’s professional experience and background give him a unique perspective on the importance of having an attorney who can navigate through the complexities of U.S. immigration laws armed with knowledge and compassion, whether fighting in immigration court to keep families united, assisting dreamers, or guiding families through hardship waiver applications.

Over the years, Mr. Vicario has volunteered at several Chicago nonprofit community organizations serving the immigrant community, including Latinos Progresando, the Illinois Coalition for Immigrant and Refugee Rights (ICIRR), and Erie Neighborhood House. He is a member of the American Immigration Lawyers Association (AILA) and the Hispanic Lawyers Association of Illinois (HLAI). While attending law school, Mr. Vicario joined Latinos Progresando’s legal staff as an intern assisting victims of domestic violence and individuals seeking family-based immigration benefits. Mr. Vicario has been an invited speaker on immigration topics, including DACA and immigration court.

Awards and Honors

Honors

CALI Excellence for the Future Award, Legal Writing IV: Immigration and Nationality Law, 2012

attorneys.name: Laura Voegeli Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Maryville, IL
attorneys.bio:
Finding a family law attorney can be stressful, and as a client you want to ensure you find a diligent lawyer to represent you. Laura Voegeli is a compassionate and caring Associate Attorney for Stange Law Firm, PC, working from the firm's Maryville, Illinois office located in Madison County. She is currently licensed to practice law in Illinois.

Laura graduated with a Bachelor of Science in Elementary Education and Spanish from the University of Wisconsin. She went on to earn her Juris Doctorate from the University of Wisconsin Law School. While in law school, she worked as a Judicial Intern at the Wisconsin Court of Appeals, where she conducted research and drafted memos, opinions, and questions in preparation for oral arguments. She also worked as a Law Clerk for a firm in Madison, Wisconsin, where she gained experience drafting pleadings, mediation statements, and briefs for personal injury cases.

Prior to joining Stange Law Firm, Laura worked at a firm in Chicago, Illinois as an Associate Attorney working on a variety of cases. She worked on family-based immigration and removal defense, including filing waivers, asylum, cancellation of removal, and bond. From there she worked for a firm in St. Louis, Missouri, again representing clients in family-based immigration matters. She conducted daily intake calls, attended client interviews in different states, and prepared and filed mandamus lawsuits.

Outside of her legal practice, Laura enjoys alpine skiing, waterskiing, and rollerblading. She also currently coaches a youth alpine ski team at Hidden Valley Ski Resort in Eureka, Missouri.

Disclaimer: The choice of a lawyer is an important decision and should not be based solely upon advertisements. Kirk C. Stange and Stange Law Firm, PC are responsible for the content. Principal place of business 120 S. Central Avenue, Suite 450, St. Louis (Clayton), MO 63105.

attorneys.bio:
At the Law Offices of Jeffery M. Leving, Ltd., Matt Volk brings his extensive experience in family law matters and strategic mind to successfully represent our clients in highly contentious and complex matrimonial, child custody, child support and Order of Protection cases.

For the past ten years, Matt's practice has focused exclusively on family law, including divorce, custody, visitation and parenting time, parentage, child support, and Order of Protection cases. Through his outstanding trial skills and painstaking preparation, Matt obtained successful resolutions for his clients and gained substantial experience as a matrimonial litigator.

Prior to focusing on family law, Matt worked in the area of civil litigation, handling a wide variety of cases before Judges and juries in Cook County and the surrounding counties. He also served at the Office of the Illinois Appellate Defender, where he handled very complex criminal matters. In this position, Matt zealously represented clients in serious criminal cases before the Illinois Appellate Court, gaining invaluable litigation experience which he now uses to benefit our clients.

Matt is passionately dedicated to achieving the best possible results for our clients through creative strategic planning and fierce advocacy.

attorneys.name: Richard S. Volpe
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
Richard S. Volpe has been practicing law in field of personal injury since November of 1980. After graduating from DePaul University College of Law, he accepted a position with the City of Chicago Corporation Counsels Office. There he handled the defense of personal injury cases filed against the City of Chicago in the Law Division of the Circuit Court of Cook County. He tried juries to verdict in cases involving slip and falls on city sidewalks, police shootings, auto accidents involving police and fire department vehicles, paramedic negligence, and defective design cases.

Mr. Volpe then switched sides and began representing people who had been injured in accidents while working at the firm of Nevoral, Corrigan and O’Connor. There he continued to expand his jury trial experience handling cases involving product liability, medical malpractice, dram shop, and many other types of accidents. Mr. Volpe continued representing individuals who were injured due to the negligence of others until 1993.

Mr. Volpe then became associated with the firm of Aronson, Smith and Cross which represented insurance companies such as Fireman’s Fund and Interstate Insurance. It was here that Mr. Volpe and Mr. Grazian first practiced law together. While with Aronson, Smith and Cross, Mr. Volpe successfully defended million dollar claims against corporation and governmental bodies such as the Metropolitan Pier and Exposition Authority. Some of those cases were notable enough to garner front page coverage in the Chicago Law Bulletin. It was also here that Mr. Volpe first started appearing before the Illinois Workers’ Compensation Commission on a regular basis. He handled the defense of employers in Workers’ Compensation matters in Chicago, Rockford, Waukegan, Joliet, Woodstock, Wheaton, and the entire State of Illinois.

Mr. Grazian and Mr. Volpe left that firm in 1998 to once again focus on representing individuals who had been injured in accidents. They have continued to practice law together since that time. The firm of Grazian and Volpe, P.C. concentrates its practice in helping the individual who has been injured whether at work or due to the negligence of some person or company. Together their years of jury trial experience have garnered millions of dollars for their clients.

Today, Mr. Volpe is considered very well known for his successes and expansive practice at the Industrial Commission as he currently handles caseloads of hundreds of Worker’s Compensation cases for Grazian & Volpe clients. Mr. Volpe has a reputation for quickly and fairly resolving Worker’s Compensation claims and is often referred such cases by physicians and attorneys in the Chicagoland area. He has served as a guest lecturer on the subject of Litigation Strategy and Technique at DePaul University College of Law.

Mr. Volpe is a member of the Workers’ Compensation Lawyers Association, The American Trial Lawyers Association, and The Illinois Bar Association. He has handled cases in Illinois trial courts as well as the Appellate Courts. In addition to the state courts, Mr. Volpe is a member of The Trial Bar of the United States District Court for the Northern District of Illinois. He has often served as Panel Chairmen for the Circuit Court of Cook County Mandatory Arbitration Program which resolves personal injury claims. In addition, he is an Arbitrator for the American Arbitration Association.

attorneys.name: Steve A. Wade
attorneys.practice_type: Probate including decedent’s estate administration and guardianships Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
Steve serves the general practice needs of our clients. He has 29 years of experience in representing families and individuals in a variety of areas. He has handled dozens of probate estates, guardianships and trust administrations. Steve has helped many families gain peace of mind by assisting them with drafting their estate planning documents. He also represents clients in residential real estate sales and purchases. Steve takes pride in serving our clients in a professional and efficient manner while always keeping an eye on achieving practical results.

In addition to heading our general practice department, Steve represents employees who have been unlawfully discriminated against, harassed or retaliated against because of their race, sex, religion, disability, age or other protected class. His practice also includes FMLA cases or have terminated workers in retaliation for exercising their rights under federal or state law.

Settlements:

$193,750 in a sexual harassment and retaliatory discharge case where an employee at a Harley Davidson dealership was subjected to harassment by other employees and terminated when she complained about it.

$122,500 in an FMLA case where an employee was told he had leave available and then was fired while on leave because the employer had made a mistake in calculating the amount of leave he had left.

$96,000 in a disability discrimination case where employer refused to accommodate the worker’s injury.

$75,000 in a racial discrimination case where a supervisor called an employee racist names.

$68,250.00 in a retaliatory discharge case where the employer fired a worker who had filed a Worker’s Compensation claim against the employer’s predecessor company.

$62,500.00 in a discrimination and retaliation case where an employee at a big-box store was subjected to harassment based on his ethnicity and disability and fired when he complained about it.

Steve takes pride in serving our clients in a professional and efficient manner while always keeping an eye on achieving practical results.

In addition to heading our general practice department, Steve represents employees who have been unlawfully discriminated against, harassed or retaliated against because of their race, sex, religion, disability, age or other protected class. His practice also includes FMLA cases or have terminated workers in retaliation for exercising their rights under federal or state law.

Settlements:

$193,750 in a sexual harassment and retaliatory discharge case where an employee at a Harley Davidson dealership was subjected to harassment by other employees and terminated when she complained about it.

$122,500 in an FMLA case where an employee was told he had leave available and then was fired while on leave because the employer had made a mistake in calculating the amount of leave he had left.

$96,000 in a disability discrimination case where employer refused to accommodate the worker’s injury.

$75,000 in a racial discrimination case where a supervisor called an employee racist names.

$68,250.00 in a retaliatory discharge case where the employer fired a worker who had filed a Worker’s Compensation claim against the employer’s predecessor company.

$62,500.00 in a discrimination and retaliation case where an employee at a big-box store was subjected to harassment based on his ethnicity and disability and fired when he complained about it.

attorneys.name: Anuj K. Wadhwa
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
Anuj Wadhwa is an associate at Rakoczy Molino Mazzochi Siwik LLP. He is registered to practice before the United States Patent and Trademark Office, and holds a degree in biochemistry.

Litigation

Mr. Wadhwa has extensive experience in all aspects of litigation, including pre-filing investigations, discovery, motion practice, Markman hearings, and pre-trial and trial practice. He has conducted and defended depositions, drafted and argued motions, prepared witnesses and experts, and appeared in court for status and motion hearings. His work encompasses a wide variety of pharmaceutical patents and technologies, and he is involved in all areas of the firm's patent litigation practice.

Opinion Writing, Patent Prosecution, and Legal Counseling

Mr. Wadhwa also is involved in the firm's patent counseling work. He has drafted numerous opinions of counsel, including non-infringement, invalidity, right-to-make and freedom to operate opinions. Mr. Wadhwa regularly assists clients in making patentability assessments, evaluating competitive patent portfolios, and conducting prior art searches. He also has extensive experience in counseling clients with respect to their patent portfolio strategies, and preparing and prosecuting patent applications.

Mr. Wadhwa has experience with various technological fields, including pharmaceutical compositions, DNA sequencing, protein synthesis, neocartilage, polymer chemistry, organic and inorganic chemistry, medical devices, chemical packaging, food products, nutritional supplements, mechanical systems, gypsum panels, lighting assemblies, electroluminescent compounds, sporting goods equipment, Internet authentication systems, business methods, and software systems.

Previous Experience

Prior to joining RMMS, Mr. Wadhwa previously was an associate at Greer, Burns & Crain, Ltd. Prior to attending law school, he worked as a laboratory assistant for Milette, Vander Wood & Associates, where he conducted laboratory research for pharmaceutical companies to determine compliance with FDA regulations for experimental drugs and devices.

attorneys.bio:
A lifelong resident of Illinois, Mr. Waldman raised his family in the Pekin/Peoria area where he resides today. Mr. Waldman attended Southern Illinois University in Carbondale, graduating with University Honors with a Bachelors degree in Political Science and Paralegal Studies. He began practicing law after graduating from University of Illinois College of Law in 1988. After law school Mr. Waldman began working for a law firm that primarily did work for insurance companies, defending personal injuries and workers compensation claims. Trying to save insurance companies money at the expense of innocent accident victims was not very rewarding. He joined Kanoski Bresney in 1994 and has worked tirelessly for injured victims ever since. It is estimated that Mr. Waldman has successfully fought for more than 10,000 injured people since coming to Kanoski Bresney.

Mr. Waldman is an avid NASCAR fan and a craft beer enthusiast.

attorneys.name: Diane Walker
attorneys.practice_type: Business Lawyers in Downers Grove, IL
attorneys.bio:
Diane Walker is the Managing Partner and a founding partner of Walker Roberts LLP. Diane has developed broad and deep expertise in complex employment law and general commercial litigation, multi-party actions, healthcare and commercial transactions.

Diane also acts as the principal business and corporate attorney for many of her clients where she counsels her clients on business formations; contract negotiations and review; mergers and acquisitions; governmental audits by the U.S. Department of Labor, Office of Contract Compliance Programs (OFCCP), the Occupational Safety and Hazard Administration (OSHA) and other federal, state and local governmental agencies; business disputes and litigation. Diane has extensive experience serving as counsel to management for employers of all sizes, including public companies, closely held businesses, nonprofit organizations and partnerships. Diane's national practice includes litigation in federal and state courts, as well as representation of employers before governmental agencies, including the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC), U.S. Department of Labor (DOL) and state human rights commissions.

Diane has extensive employment litigation experience, including lead counsel designation representing employers in pattern and practice lawsuits brought by the EEOC and multi-plaintiff cases under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act. Throughout her career, she has successfully defended employers in a variety of employment disputes, including wrongful termination and discrimination claims, retaliatory discharge actions, misclassification of employees under the Fair Labor Standards Act, reasonable accommodation claims under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), non-compete/trade secret litigation, wage and hour audits, breach of employment contracts, and tortuous interference claims.

Diane has successfully litigated precedent-setting employment cases and been notably successful in securing summary disposition of employment litigation and dismissal of charges before federal and state agencies.

In addition to traditional litigation matters, Diane regularly counsels employers on statutory compliance with employment statutes, affirmative action compliance programs, union avoidance techniques, collective bargaining and arbitration matters, employee handbooks, plant closings and relocations, employment contracts, and sensitive personnel policies, including drug-testing and sexual harassment, as well as other employment related issues. Diane routinely performs internal human resources audits targeting areas relative to human resources management and organizational development, including wage and hour compliance; time off and leaves; education and training; health and safety; and hiring, performance and termination.

Diane develops and reviews existing employee handbooks and management policies and procedure manuals designed to ensure compliance with state and federal statutes and regulations and to build effective employee relations and minimize or eliminate risk exposure. She has presented on a variety of employment issues and develops and conducts individual and group training sessions on topics such as the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), the ADA, the Age Discrimination in Employment Act, the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA), sexual harassment, and hiring and termination issues.

attorneys.name: Charles A. Wallace
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
Charles graduated from John Marshall Law School and was subsequently appointed an Assistant Attorney General in 1994. He spent the next five years handling complex litigation matters in both federal and state courts. His specialty was defending civil rights lawsuits brought by incarcerated felons and represented by federally appointed ‘brown-shoe’ law firms. Although, at such an early point in his career, he was trying cases against some of the most renown and accomplished trial lawyers in Chicago, Charles won every case he litigated. When he wasn’t on trial, Charles was what was called a ‘fireman’. Meaning that he was called upon to handle many of the most potentially explosive motions and court appearances across the state. Charles argued successfully on behalf of his clients in more than 15 counties and federal districts across Illinois.

By 1999, Charles had developed a reputation as a trial lawyer that the private sector couldn’t ignore. He was sought out and given offers to leave public service, ultimately spending an eternity working for one year on the side of the insurance defense industry before finding his true calling as a plaintiff’s lawyer. In 2000 Charles joined a very well respected and accomplished solo practitioner and spent the next seven years under the direct tutelage of a consummate trial attorney. He handled all aspects of their cases, from the discovery phase to trial to appellate arguments.

In 2007, Charles joined the Morici, Figlioli & Associates family and has thrived in the courtroom on behalf of our clients. Charles has settled cases well in excess of seven figures on behalf of our clients, but his true talents lie in the courtroom. One example is a trial that Charles orchestrated on behalf of an injured iron worker during which the insurance carrier raised their monetary offer each day at the conclusion of testimony until the iron worker could no longer resist the amount of money and settled. Adversaries who haven’t been prescient enough to offer acceptable settlements to Charles’ clients have regretted it. Such as the defendant general contractor who lost their appeal of Charles’ $1.8m verdict for a mason who fell from his own scaffolding and injured his back.

As one judge opined of Charles' ability after presiding over a two week trial, ‘he has an innate ability in the courtroom, you can't teach what he does.' Charles believes deeply that with such an ability comes a tremendous responsibility to work as hard as possible to advocate on behalf of his clients. In twenty years of practice, Charles has already won ten jury verdicts in excess of a million dollars and played an integral role in amassing more than $40 million in verdicts and settlements on behalf of his clients. Charles has earned admission into the National Million Dollar and Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum and Illinois' prestigious, invitation only, Society of Trial Lawyers.

Charles grew up in Rock Island, Illinois, where his father practiced law for more than 50 years. Charles’ wife, Ashley, is also an attorney and in their free time they enjoy caring for their animals and working for numerous animal charities. They insist on making time to travel, but are admittedly too lax about making time for tennis and other exercises they enjoy.

attorneys.name: Dawn L. Wall
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial and Business Litigation Lawyers in Bloomington, IL
attorneys.bio:
Expertise

Ms. Wall has practiced law in Central Illinois for over twenty-five years. Her areas of expertise include representing corporate clients in commercial and business litigation matters as well as employment related matters. Ms. Wall also manages workers' compensation claims for injured workers and self-insured employers. Ms. Wall has successfully argued cases before the Illinois Supreme Court, the Appellate Courts of Illinois, the U.S. District Courts in the Central and Northern Districts and the Seventh Circuit Court of Appeals.

Background & Education

A native of Yorkville, Illinois, Ms. Wall obtained her Bachelor of Science degree cum laude from Kentucky Wesleyan College in 1984. She received her Juris Doctorate degree from Southern Illinois University in 1987. She is presently a partner with the firm, having joined the firm in 1987.

Professional Associations & Memberships

Ms. Wall is a member of the Illinois State Bar Association, the Mclean County Bar Association and a member of the Robert C. Underwood Inn of Court.

Community Activities

Ms. Wall has been an active member of Prairie State Legal Services. She has served on the Advisory Council of Prairie State Legal Services and was recognized as the “Volunteer of the Year” by Prairie State Legal Services. She has served as a Board Member of Victim Offender Reconciliation Program “VORP” of McLean County and has served as a mediator and arbitrator in McLean County. She is also a past member of the Bloomington Rotary Club.

attorneys.name: Edward A. Wallace
attorneys.practice_type: Mass Tort Litigation Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
Ed joined the firm in February 2000, soon after its founding by Ken Wexler. Since then, he has helped lead the firm to national prominence. He became a partner in 2003. Ed focuses his practice on complex multi-party litigation, and he has been appointed to leadership positions in numerous high-profile cases, including recent appointments in securities and mass tort litigation. Ed has been critical in the development of the firm's mass tort practice and, in the process, he has gained a national reputation for integrity, efficiency, strategic planning, understanding the relevant science, and achieving success.

In the inaugural edition of Benchmark Plaintiff, The Definitive Guide to America's Leading Plaintiff Firms & Attorneys honored him as a "Local Litigation Star" in its Illinois rankings in consumer protection. He has received this honor in 2012, 2013 and 2014. In 2014, Ed also was named an Illinois Super Lawyer, an honor given to no more than 5 percent of attorneys in the state. He was recognized as a "Rising Star" by Super Lawyers for the practice areas of class actions and mass torts in 2009. Ed was rated by peers in the Bar and given an AV Preeminent rating by Martindale-Hubbell, the highest rating a lawyer can obtain, indicating a very high to preeminent legal ability and exceptional ethical standards.

James H. Waller has been with Johnson Law Group since 2006. Mr. Waller is an aggressive and experienced trial attorney, and has substantial experience with appeals, expungements, and pardons. Specifically, Mr. Waller's work for DUI clients has helped redefine DUI defense in Central Illinois. James has handled many high-profile cases for the firm, from shootings to major Class X drug-trafficking cases. Whether you need a quick resolution to your criminal case under the best possible terms, or an aggressive, knock-down, drag-out jury trial, James Waller will provide you with top-shelf representation and personal attention.

James earned his Bachelor's in Computer Science in 2000 and worked for tech startups here in the Midwest, helping to create and build companies like 321 Studios and Lashback. As these companies became pioneers in wider Intellectual Property and cyberlaw issues, James was attracted to the practice of law and its intersection with technology. He graduated from the University of Illinois College of law (early) in December 2006 and has been with Johnson Law Group since. As online technology has become inherent to every aspect of our lives, so has James's study and practice of it grown to include Criminal Defense, Family Law, Civil Litigation, Trademark and Copyright licensing, etc. James is licensed in the State of Illinois and the Central District of Illinois. James is a father of two, is also a successful game designer and producer of mobile Apps and family games.

attorneys.name: Christopher J. Warmbold
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in St Charles, IL
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Christopher J. Warmbold has dedicated his legal career to representing those who are often marginalized, overlooked, and underrepresented. He has a successful track record of advocating on behalf of his injured clients that was earned by standing up to insurance companies who fail or refuse to uphold their obligation to provide full compensation for the harms caused by the negligence of others. Chris concentrates his practice in matters of personal injury involving medical malpractice, motor accidents, wrongful death, and general civil litigation.

"Coming from a family of blue-collar workers taught me the importance of hard work and standing up for your neighbor – lessons i have not forgotten. All my clients can count on having a zealous advocate in their corner, fighting to level the playing field for them in the pursuit of justice."

Chris is a graduate of Northern Illinois University where he received his bachelor’s degree in economics cum laude and he later returned to NIU and obtained his law degree in 2013. That same year he was licensed to practice in the State of Illinois.

Prior to joining Meyers & Flowers, Chris worked for the Kendall County Public Defender’s Office where he represented the accused and fought against the power and influence of the State’s Attorney’s Office. As a criminal defense attorney, Chris spent countless hours in the courtroom providing high quality representation to his clients charged with serious offenses while simultaneously fighting to limit their exposure to collateral consequences. After a successful career as a defense attorney, Chris joined a well-respected law firm in Aurora, Illinois where he gained invaluable experience as a plaintiff’s trial lawyer. He then joined Meyers & Flowers in 2022.

Chris is an experienced litigator having successfully tried both criminal and civil cases to verdict. A notable victory came in September of 2021, when Chris and a fellow attorney secured a $7.7 million verdict for the family of a 33-year-old woman who died because her treating physician failed to recognize, prevent, and treat a thiamine deficiency that developed following bariatric surgery. The verdict stands as one of the largest ever awarded in Winnebago County history.

In addition to being a successful trial lawyer, Chris has invaluable experience challenging adverse outcomes and safeguarding circuit court victories in the 2nd District Appellate Court. Recently, Chris had the distinct privilege to argue a case before the Illinois Supreme Court where he advocated for judicial recognition of critical safeguards for disabled wards concerning their right to marry. The breadth of Chris’ experience as a legal writer, trial lawyer and appellate advocate has earned him recognition from his peers in the legal community, including recognition as a Super Lawyers “Rising Star”. The Rising Stars list recognizes no more than 2.5 percent of attorneys in each state, either under the age of 40 or in practice for 10 years or less.

Chris is a member of the Illinois State Bar Association, Illinois Trial Lawyers Association, Kane County Bar Association, and Kendall County Bar Association where he formally served as President.

Chris was raised in McHenry County and currently resides in suburban Cook County with his wife and two sons. When not devoting his time and efforts to his clients, Chris serves as a mentor to NIU law students helping guide them through the intricacies of law school, legal internships, the bar exam, and life as a practicing lawyer.

attorneys.name: Michael J Warner
attorneys.practice_type: Wrongful Death Lawyers in Moline, IL
attorneys.bio:
Michael J. Warner has practiced personal injury law for more than 30 years. He is admired among his peers for his excellent legal ability and extreme ethical standards. He is known for being an aggressive litigator and has relentlessly dedicated himself to representing injured persons and the estates of people wrongfully killed due to medical malpractice, construction and trucking accidents, motor vehicles collisions. He continues to obtain seven figure settlements and large verdicts against hospitals, physicians and others responsible for causing injury or wrongful death. Not only has Michael J. Warner tried and resolved complex cases, he is a regular litigator for the Illinois Trial Lawyers Association, of which he has been a member since 1974, on personal injury matters.

Birth trauma, obstetric and pediatric malpractice cases are of special interest to his law firm. He is a member of the Birth Trauma Litigation Committee of the American Association for Justice (formerly known as American Trial Lawyers Association). This group regularly discusses strategies in handling birth trauma litigation and recent advances in medicine and science.

Michael J. Warner is an advocate for trial by jury and is a tireless lobbyist against corporate interests and the insurance industry who is trying to destroy the rights of citizens to obtain fair compensation for their injuries.

Mr. Warner was appointed in 2001 by the Illinois Supreme Court to serve on the Illinois Pattern Jury Instructions Committee. This committee drafts the jury instructions which are given to all civil juries in the State of Illinois.

attorneys.name: Jamie E. Weiss
attorneys.practice_type: Class Action Lawyers in Highland Park, IL
attorneys.bio:
Jamie E. Weiss is a founding partner of Quantum Legal LLC with more than a decade of experience working in antitrust, securities and consumer class actions, and personal injury cases. Jamie is the managing partner at Quantum Legal LLC, and is actively involved in the firm's long-term growth and strategic development.

Jamie attended Indiana University, receiving Bachelors of Art in Psychology and Telecommunications. She received her Juris Doctorate from Chicago-Kent College of Law-Illinois Institute of Technology in 1995, and also earned a Certificate in Environmental Law. Jamie is admitted to state and federal courts within Illinois and is also a member of the District of Colorado and the bar of the Supreme Court of the United States.

Prior to joining Quantum Legal LLC, Jamie worked for the Law Offices of Eric D. Freed on antitrust and securities class action cases, including High Fructose Corn Syrup litigation, Commercial Explosives litigation, and Prudential Life Practices cases. Prior to that, Jamie specialized in toxic torts at a boutique plaintiffs' personal injury firm in Chicago. Jamie is actively involved in environmental issues, animal sheltering and animal rights, and is a member of the Animal Legal Defense Fund. She has performed pro bono work on behalf of area animal shelters and sits on the Board of Illinois Cocker Spaniel and Small Dog Rescue. Jamie lobbies on behalf of protection for animals in many settings including wild mustangs, performing animals, spay and neuter campaigns, and a halt to cruel and unnecessary animal testing and puppy mills, among other causes.

Jamie's memberships include WWF, PETA, NWF, the Ocean Conservancy, HSUS, ASPCA, Last Chance for Animals, Alley Cat Allies, Rainforest Alliance, Greenpeace, NAVS, AVAR, various Mustang and Premarin horse rescue groups, as well as area animal shelters.

World Wildlife Fund

WWF's mission is the conservation of nature. Using the best available scientific knowledge and advancing that knowledge, the World Wildlife Find works to preserve the diversity and abundance of life on Earth and the health of ecological systems. www.wwf.org

Animal Legal Defense Fund

For more than a quarter-century, the Animal Legal Defense Fund has been fighting to protect the lives and advance the interests of animals through the legal system. www.aldf.org

Last Chance for Animals Last Chance for Animals (LCA)

LCA recognizes that animals have the ability to experience pain, and as such they deserve certain basic rights protecting them from pain caused by humans. LCA believes that non-human animals should not be subjected to suffering and exploitation by humans because alternatives exist for nearly every traditional "usage" of animals. www.lcanimal.org

Rainforest Alliance

The Rainforest Alliance works to conserve biodiversity and ensure sustainable livelihoods by transforming land-

use practices, business practices and consumer behavior. www.rainforest-alliance.org

People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals

PETA is dedicated to establishing and protecting the rights of all animals. PETA operates under the simple principle that animals are not ours to eat, wear, experiment on, or use for entertainment. www.peta.org

Best Friends Animal Sanctuary

Best Friends Animal Society runs the nation's largest sanctuary for abused and abandoned animals. Best Friends operates a low-cost spay/neuter program. www.bestfriends.org

The Ocean Conservancy

Ocean Conservancy promotes healthy and diverse ocean ecosystems and opposes practices that threaten ocean life and human life. Through research, education, and science-based advocacy, Ocean Conservancy informs, inspires, and empowers people to speak and act on behalf of the oceans. Ocean Conservancy strives to be the world's foremost advocate for the oceans. www.oceanconservancy.org

The Humane Society of the United States

The Humane Society of the United States seeks a humane and sustainable world for all animals-a world that will also benefit people: Celebrating Animals, Confronting Cruelty. www.hsus.org

The Fund for Animals

The Fund for Animals carries on the legacy of Cleveland Amory with the hard-hitting programs for which it has been known for 4 decades, and with a renewed emphasis on hands-on animal care services. www.fundforanimals.org

Ally Cat Allies

Through outreach, education, and community building, Alley Cat Allies serves as the expert on Trap-Neuter-Return and supports the efforts of citizens humanely caring for cats. www.alleycat.org

National Anti-Vivisection Society

The National Anti-Vivisection Society is a national, not-for-profit educational organization incorporated in the State of Illinois. NAVS promotes greater compassion, respect and justice for animals through educational programs based on respected ethical and scientific theory and supported by extensive documentation of the cruelty and waste of vivisection. www.navs.org

Greenpeace

Greenpeace's mission is to bear witness to environmental destruction in a peaceful, non-violent manner. Greenpeace use non-violent confrontation to raise the level and quality of public debate. They expose threats to the environment and find solutions they have no permanent allies or adversaries and ensures financial independence from political or commercial interests. Greenpeace seeks solutions for, and promote open, informed debate about society's environmental choices. www.greenpeace.org

Doris Day Animal League

The Doris Day Animal League works to improve the humane treatment of animals by lobbying to pass new laws and enforce existing laws that reduce the suffering of animals. www.ddal.org

Petfinder

Petfinder is an on-line, searchable database of animals that need homes and a directory of over 10,000 animal shelters and adoption organizations across the USA, Canada and Mexico. www.petfinder.com

Farm Sanctuary

Farm Sanctuary works to end cruelty to farm animals and promotes compassionate living through rescue, education and advocacy. www.farmsanctuary.org

Lifesavers Wild Horse Rescue

Dedicated to saving American mustangs and domestic horses from abuse, neglect & slaughter. www.wildhorserescue.org

She has performed pro bono work on behalf of area animal shelters and sits on the Board of Illinois Cocker Spaniel and Small Dog Rescue. Jamie lobbies on behalf of protection for animals in many settings including wild mustangs, performing animals, spay and neuter campaigns, and a halt to cruel and unnecessary animal testing and puppy mills, among other causes.

Jamie's memberships include WWF, PETA, NWF, the Ocean Conservancy, HSUS, ASPCA, Last Chance for Animals, Alley Cat Allies, Rainforest Alliance, Greenpeace, NAVS, AVAR, various Mustang and Premarin horse rescue groups, as well as area animal shelters.

World Wildlife Fund

WWF's mission is the conservation of nature. Using the best available scientific knowledge and advancing that knowledge, the World Wildlife Find works to preserve the diversity and abundance of life on Earth and the health of ecological systems. www.wwf.org

Animal Legal Defense Fund

For more than a quarter-century, the Animal Legal Defense Fund has been fighting to protect the lives and advance the interests of animals through the legal system. www.aldf.org

Last Chance for Animals Last Chance for Animals (LCA)

LCA recognizes that animals have the ability to experience pain, and as such they deserve certain basic rights protecting them from pain caused by humans. LCA believes that non-human animals should not be subjected to suffering and exploitation by humans because alternatives exist for nearly every traditional "usage" of animals. www.lcanimal.org

Rainforest Alliance

The Rainforest Alliance works to conserve biodiversity and ensure sustainable livelihoods by transforming land-

use practices, business practices and consumer behavior. www.rainforest-alliance.org

People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals

PETA is dedicated to establishing and protecting the rights of all animals. PETA operates under the simple principle that animals are not ours to eat, wear, experiment on, or use for entertainment. www.peta.org

Best Friends Animal Sanctuary

Best Friends Animal Society runs the nation's largest sanctuary for abused and abandoned animals. Best Friends operates a low-cost spay/neuter program. www.bestfriends.org

The Ocean Conservancy

Ocean Conservancy promotes healthy and diverse ocean ecosystems and opposes practices that threaten ocean life and human life. Through research, education, and science-based advocacy, Ocean Conservancy informs, inspires, and empowers people to speak and act on behalf of the oceans. Ocean Conservancy strives to be the world's foremost advocate for the oceans. www.oceanconservancy.org

The Humane Society of the United States

The Humane Society of the United States seeks a humane and sustainable world for all animals-a world that will also benefit people: Celebrating Animals, Confronting Cruelty. www.hsus.org

The Fund for Animals

The Fund for Animals carries on the legacy of Cleveland Amory with the hard-hitting programs for which it has been known for 4 decades, and with a renewed emphasis on hands-on animal care services. www.fundforanimals.org

Ally Cat Allies

Through outreach, education, and community building, Alley Cat Allies serves as the expert on Trap-Neuter-Return and supports the efforts of citizens humanely caring for cats. www.alleycat.org

National Anti-Vivisection Society

The National Anti-Vivisection Society is a national, not-for-profit educational organization incorporated in the State of Illinois. NAVS promotes greater compassion, respect and justice for animals through educational programs based on respected ethical and scientific theory and supported by extensive documentation of the cruelty and waste of vivisection. www.navs.org

Greenpeace

Greenpeace's mission is to bear witness to environmental destruction in a peaceful, non-violent manner. Greenpeace use non-violent confrontation to raise the level and quality of public debate. They expose threats to the environment and find solutions they have no permanent allies or adversaries and ensures financial independence from political or commercial interests. Greenpeace seeks solutions for, and promote open, informed debate about society's environmental choices. www.greenpeace.org

Doris Day Animal League

The Doris Day Animal League works to improve the humane treatment of animals by lobbying to pass new laws and enforce existing laws that reduce the suffering of animals. www.ddal.org

Petfinder

Petfinder is an on-line, searchable database of animals that need homes and a directory of over 10,000 animal shelters and adoption organizations across the USA, Canada and Mexico. www.petfinder.com

Farm Sanctuary

Farm Sanctuary works to end cruelty to farm animals and promotes compassionate living through rescue, education and advocacy. www.farmsanctuary.org

Lifesavers Wild Horse Rescue

attorneys.name: David Weiss
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
David Weiss is a unquestionable powerhouse in the courtroom and a razor-sharp legal strategist behind the scenes. As a Partner at Taege Law Offices, David blends formidable trial experience with a deep command of the law, making him a uniquely effective advocate in highly complex family law litigation. He shines when the issues are tough, the facts are muddled, and the stakes are high, making him incredibly adept at guiding his clients through their family law matters.

David has a calm, confident presence that resonates with judges and clients alike. He excels in both trial and appellate advocacy, with a courtroom demeanor that is equal parts composed, commanding, and persuasive. Whether cross-examining a witness, arguing an evidentiary issue, or presenting a final argument to the court, David brings clarity and conviction to every proceeding. David’s experience across multiple practice areas, with a board history in family law, gives him a well-rounded perspective that strengthens his approach to strategy and litigation.

But David doesn’t just win by courtroom presence alone. He is a legal mind through and through, known within the firm and amongst judges for his ability to spot nuanced statutory conflicts, break down obscure procedural questions, and build layered, creative arguments. If there is a novel issue in the case, David is the person who is the first to flag it, research it, and is ready to argue. He thrives on intellectual rigor but delivers with practical, client-centered impact.

A 2014 graduate of UIC Law (formerly the John Marshall Law School), David’s passion for family law took root early, through externships with the Domestic Relations Division of the Circuit Court of Cook County and the Cook County Domestic Violence Legal Clinic. He also worked with the Veterans Legal Support Center & Clinic, deepening his commitment to service and justice. Since admission, David has led his own firm, litigated across multiple counties, and built a reputation for reliability, preparation, and results.

At Taege Law Offices, David is a cornerstone of the litigation team. Clients trust him because he is grounded, strategic, and always prepared. Colleagues value him because he is collaborative, exacting, and relentless in the right ways. When your case demands both precision and power, David is your advocate.

attorneys.name: William H. Wentz
attorneys.practice_type: Business Services Lawyers in Wheaton, IL
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Wentz advises and represents privately-held companies, from start-ups to large corporations, in the full range of business matters. He is particularly experienced in structuring transactions relating to the acquisition or sale of a business, or involving financing, licensing, employee retention and domestic or international joint ventures and partnerships.

Mr. Wentz gained national attention as a principal architect of leading antitrust cases involving the prescription drug industry and as the founder of one of the first e-commerce companies. Early in his legal career, he served as Associate General Counsel of the Civil Aeronautics Board in charge of the Board's litigation and enforcement during airline deregulation. Prior to the CAB, he was an attorney-advisor to two Chairmen of the Federal Trade Commission.

For the past two decades, Mr. Wentz's primary interest has been privately-held businesses. He started the Entrepreneurial Roundtable for the University of Chicago's Graduate School of Business in 1991 and still serves as its chief Coordinator. He was also one of the founders of the MBBI, the leading organization of professionals in the Midwest concerned with mergers and acquisitions.

attorneys.name: Colleen Wengler
attorneys.practice_type: Guardianship Lawyers in Joliet, IL
attorneys.bio:
Colleen has been practicing in the Joliet area since 2003, with experience in civil litigation, trust and estate litigation, decedent’s estates, guardianships and estate planning. During that time, Colleen has focused her practice in trust and estate litigation and guardianships. Colleen has represented many trustees, executors, administrators, guardians, heirs and beneficiaries. Colleen has also served as a guardian ad litem for numerous minors and alleged disabled adults during that time. Colleen, along with co-presenters Lisa Kinser and Frank Hauenschild, teaches a seminar regarding the role of the guardian ad litem in probate court for attorneys seeking to apply for appointments as guardians ad litem in the Twelfth Judicial Circuit, in Will County, Illinois.

Colleen was appointed Will County Public Guardian and Will County Public Administrator by Governor Bruce Rauner on February 2, 2018 and currently serves in those capacities. In her role as Public Guardian, Colleen serves as the Guardian of the Person and/or Estate of Disabled Persons in Will County that do not have family members willing or able to serve. In her role as Public Administrator, Colleen accepts appointments by the Probate Court to serve as the Administrator of Decedent’s Estates for which there is no appropriate Administrator willing or able to Serve.

Colleen has been certified as a National Certified Guardian by the Center for Guardianship Certification. Colleen is also a Certified Dementia Practitioner.

attorneys.name: Alison J. Wetzel
attorneys.practice_type: Business Services Lawyers in Wheaton, IL
attorneys.bio:
Alison J. Wetzel is an experienced transactional attorney in the firm's Business Services practice group. Over the course of her career, Alison has acted as a trusted legal advisor to privately-held businesses across diverse industries, providing practical solutions and risk-balanced advice on day-to-day legal and business issues.

In her practice, Alison handles a wide variety of business transactions, including acquisitions and divestitures, commercial contracts, business planning and commercial financing transactions. She is skilled at drafting and negotiating a wide variety of complex commercial contracts, including manufacturing, supply, vendor, distributor, non-disclosure, licensing, information technology, construction, engineering services, consulting, professional services and master services agreements.

Alison is also experienced in representing buyers and sellers in acquisition and divestiture transactions, including conducting due diligence, negotiating and drafting purchase agreements and other transaction documents, and assisting with business transition matters. In addition, Alison counsels clients on entity formation matters, including entity selection, shareholder agreements and operating agreements.

Alison has served as outside general counsel to privately-held businesses in a broad range of industries, including manufacturers and suppliers, construction contractors, engineering firms, software development and information technology firms, physicians and other professionals. She is an innovative business attorney who collaborates with her clients to successfully achieve their business objectives.

Prior to joining Huck Bouma, Alison served as a Partner with the Burr Ridge law firm of Goldstine, Skrodzki, Russian, Nemec and Hoff, Ltd.

attorneys.name: Kelsey Whalen
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Kelsey Whalen assists individuals who have been subjected to illegal employment practices. Ms. Whalen handles a wide range of employment issues with a primary focus in workplace discrimination, sexual harassment, and retaliation. She aims to reach the best possible resolution for her clients by working with them every step of their case and fighting on their behalf.

Ms. Whalen completed her undergraduate degree at Eastern Kentucky University, where she was a member of the Honors Program and defended her thesis on the topic of gender discrimination in the sports industry. After graduation, Ms. Whalen moved to Arizona to attend law school at Sandra Day O'Connor College of Law at Arizona State University.

Throughout law school, she clerked for an employment law firm and worked as a research assistant. She also served as a teaching assistant for Legal Writing and Legal Advocacy classes and was a member of the Law Journal for Social Justice. Upon graduation, she earned a dean's award for her achievements throughout law school.

In her free time, Ms. Whalen enjoys listening to podcasts, reading memoirs, and as a sports enthusiast, she enjoys following her favorite sports teams.

attorneys.name: Kelly K. Wheeler
attorneys.practice_type: Asbestos & Mesothelioma Lawyers in Alton, IL
attorneys.bio:
Kelly Wheeler is a mesothelioma attorney at Simmons Hanly Conroy. She brings nearly a decade of experience to her role at the firm, where she focuses on preparing cases against negligent asbestos companies.

“It’s incredibly gratifying to be able to help people who have been seriously hurt by corporate misconduct and hold those corporations accountable,” said Kelly. “It means the world to me to be able to make a real difference in the lives of my clients.”

Kelly is dedicated to fostering a strong relationship with those she represents, ensuring they receive the support, respect and compassion they deserve throughout the legal process.

A Dynamic Legal Professional

Throughout her career, Kelly has been involved in all aspects of case preparation, including briefing and arguing motions, taking depositions, issuing and responding to subpoenas, developing experts, managing discovery and more. She has also proven herself to be a strong asset on trial teams.

Her knowledge and abilities have allowed her to craft innovative case strategies that deliver favorable results for her clients.

“I enjoy the creative and strategic thinking required to work on complex legal issues, and I get to work alongside people of the highest intelligence and integrity,” she expressed.

Kelly has represented clients across many different case types, including:

Complex litigation

Opioid litigation

Mesothelioma lawsuits

Personal injury cases

She has helped secure hundreds of millions of dollars in settlements for her clients, demonstrating her ability to achieve results even in challenging cases.

Kelly also represented several State Attorneys General against opioid manufacturers, distributors and dispensers, resulting in over $1 billion recovered.

At Simmons Hanly Conroy, Kelly focuses primarily on case investigation, product discovery and depositions. Her clients can expect a dynamic partnership built upon mutual respect, honesty, transparency, and open communication.

“It’s an honor to be trusted by a client, and the client should feel confident that I appreciate and will safeguard their trust while fighting for them,” said Kelly.

Background & Experience

Kelly’s interest in becoming a lawyer began in high school, where she excelled in debate. She realized that a career in law would allow her to channel her passion for oral advocacy to make a meaningful impact in the lives of others.

In 2012, Kelly graduated from the University of Notre Dame with a degree in the Classics. She went on to attend Baylor Law School on a Dean’s Academic Excellence Scholarship and earned her J.D. in 2015.

Kelly initially focused her practice on personal injury cases, including catastrophic injuries. From there, she became the head of the pharmaceutical mass tort department at a law firm and also began working on asbestos cases. Most recently, Kelly represented states and municipalities in high-profile opioid litigation.

Kelly’s extensive experience, strong work ethic and commitment to her clients make her a valuable member of the Simmons Hanly Conroy team.

attorneys.name: John W. Whitcomb
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation & Appeals Lawyers in Chicago, IL
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Whitcomb is a partner at Monahan Law Group, LLC. Mr. Whitcomb specializes in involuntary commitment actions in Mental Health Court, guardianship and probate matters, and various litigation involving individual with mental illness and intellectual disabilities. Mr. Whitcomb has an extensive appellate practice including having argued In Re V.S., 2022 IL App (2d) 210667 (represented adopted parents ability to deny visitation to grandparents who were seeking visitation as a matter of right)); People v. Gomez-Ramrirez, 2021 IL App (3d) 200121 (represented medical center who objected to release of confidential medical records based on physician-patient privilege); and Warga v. Warga, 2015 IL App (1st) 151182 (guardian challenged the standing of a wife where the parties were seeking a divorce on behalf of a disabled person).

Mr. Whitcomb has over 35 years of experience representing clients in State and Federal trial and appellate courts. Prior to joining Monahan Law Group, Mr. Whitcomb was a Senior Attorney at Equip for Equality. In his capacity as Senior Attorney, Mr. Whitcomb represented clients in issues relating to guardianship, the Illinois Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Confidentiality Act, the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Code, and community placement of disabled individuals in the community. Mr. Whitcomb argued before the appellate court the seminal guardianship case, In Re Estate of K.E.J., on forced sterilization that eventually became the basis for the Illinois Statute, 755 ILCS 5/11a-17.1. Mr. Whitcomb also represented clients in abuse and neglect proceedings in juvenile court. Mr. Whitcomb was class counsel is several class actions regarding the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) including Access Living of Metropolitan Chicago v. Chicago Transit Authority, Ligas v. Maram, and Williams v. Quinn.

Mr. Whitcomb is the recipient of the 2012 Recipient of Access Living's "Lead On!" Award, and LAF’s 1996 and 1994 Equal Justice Award. Mr. Whitcomb is the past and current Chairperson of the Chicago Bar Association’s Mental Health and Disability Law Committee. Mr. Whitcomb has a Teacher Training Certificate with the National Institute of Trial Advocacy and has trained other lawyers in trial advocacy and deposition taking.

Mr. Whitcomb is a graduate of Tulane Law School and has a Bachelor of Arts from Oberlin College.
